ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r1.claim: Al-Qalam pairs with al-Mulk: both warn Quraysh of judgment and worldly consequences for denial, but al-Qalam uses a sterner tone and different arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r1.anchor: the difference lies in the style, nature of arguments and the tone adopted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r2.claim: Following al-Mulk’s closing challenge, al-Qalam compares the Prophet’s preaching, Book, and character with Quraysh’s corrupt leadership to show that the guided will succeed and their leaders lead them to ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p419/r2.anchor: a comparison is made in this sūrah between the preaching of the Prophet (sws), the Book presented by him and his lofty character

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r1.claim: As with Qāf at 50:1, Nūn is named in the opening; Arabic syntax suppresses the inchoative, supplied in the translation as “This is Sūrah Nūn.”
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r1.anchor: According to linguistic principles of Arabic, the mubtatadā’ (inchoative) is suppressed here

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r2.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r2.claim: Farāhī holds that the disjointed letters are names of their sūrahs used to signify meaning, though most meanings have been lost.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r2.anchor: According to him, these are names of their respective sūrahs and are used to signify some meaning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r3.claim: Nūn still means fish; its use alludes to Jonah, called the companion of the fish at the sūrah’s end and dhū al-nūn in al-Anbiyāʾ.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r3.anchor: the allusion is to the Prophet Jonah (sws) who had been swallowed by a fish

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r4.claim: The wāw is an oath, and Qur’anic oaths substantiate claims; here the oath supports three opening claims, beginning with the opponents’ folly in calling the Prophet possessed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p422/r4.anchor: such oaths are meant to substantiate a claim(s).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r1.speaker: Muj āhid
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r1.claim: Mujāhid reports that the pen is the one used to write the Qur’an and “what they write” refers to the Qur’an itself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r1.anchor: there is a narrative from Muj āhid that the word “pen” refers to the pen with which

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r2.claim: Writing is a divine favor that safeguards revelation from the corruption and loss that threatened earlier oral teachings; scripture was written, and the Qur’an was preserved against alteration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r2.anchor: In order to protect religion from this danger, the Almighty taught man the use of the pen and writing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r3.claim: In the author’s view, the pen oath means the written record of divine teachings, including earlier scriptures whose testimony supports Muhammad’s prophethood and advent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r3.anchor: it refers to all the written record of divine teachings which was preserved through the pen

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r4.claim: Context identifies “what they write” as the Qur’an being revealed and recorded by the Companions; its elevated discourse attests to Muhammad’s truthfulness, civility, and prophethood.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p423/r4.anchor: which was being revealed at that time and was being written by the Companions

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the commentators agree that this Meccan sūra is Meccan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية. قال ابن عطية: ولا خلاف فيها بين أحد من أهل التأويل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.claim: Most of the sūra was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Abū Jahl; its opening refutes accusations of madness and praises the Prophet's patience and character.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.anchor: ومعظمها نزل في الوليد بن المغيرة وأبي جهل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.claim: The sūra follows a prior account of the blessed and wretched and God's power and knowledge, answering claims that the Prophet's revelation was poetry, magic, or madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.anchor: وكان الكفار ينسبونه مرة إلى الشعر، ومرة إلى السحر، ومرة إلى الجنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r4.claim: N is one of the alphabetic disjoint letters, like Ṣād and Qāf; assigning it a grammatical case is conjecture because it is outside ordinary syntactic government.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r4.anchor: ن: حرف من حروف المعجم، نحو ص وق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid interpret N as the great fish on which the seven earths rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r5.anchor: أنه اسم الحوت الأعظم الذي عليه الأرضون السبع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r6.claim: They interpret N as an inkwell; other reports call it a tablet of light, the last letter in al-Raḥmān, or a river in Paradise, though Abū Ḥayyān doubts the reports' authenticity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا والحسن وقتادة والضحاك: أنه اسم الدواة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r7.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī says N is simply an alphabetic letter, like the other sūra openings; a complete word would be inflected like “the pen.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r7.anchor: وقال أبو نصر عبد الرحيم القشيري في تفسيره: ن حرف من حروف المعجم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r8.claim: If N means an inkwell or whale and is an object of oath, its grammatical form should reflect whether it is a masculine or feminine name or a common noun; its form does none of these.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r8.anchor: ومن قال إنه اسم الدواة أو الحوت وزعم أنه مقسم به كالقلم، فإن كان علما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says that if N means inkwell, it could be an Arabic dialect word or a borrowed term, and cites a poem about the inkwell shedding tears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r9.anchor: إذا كان اسما للدواة، فإما أن يكون لغة لبعض العرب، أو لفظة أعجمية عربت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.claim: Those who identify N with the cosmic fish take the pen as the divinely created pen recording decrees and “they write” as angels; those who take N as a name identify the familiar pen and human writers, citing Ibn ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.anchor: فمن جعله البهموت، جعل القلم هو الذي خلقه الله وأمره بكتب الكائنات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.claim: The oath presents writing as a foundation of knowledge and worldly and otherworldly affairs; the pen is a universal divine blessing and companion to speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.anchor: فإن القلم أخو اللسان ونعمة من الله عامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r12.claim: Most read N with a still nūn assimilated into the wāw of والقلم, with or without nasalization; several canonical readers pronounce it clearly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r12.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ن بسكون النون وإدغامها في واو والقلم بغنة وقوم بغير غنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق والحسن وأبو السمال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r13.claim: They read the nūn with kasra to resolve two adjacent still consonants; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĪsā also report a fatḥa reading, with alternative grammatical explanations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق والحسن وأبو السمال: بكسر النون لالتقاء الساكنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.claim: ما may be relative or a verbal noun; the pronoun in “they write” may refer to the written book signaled by the pen, meaning recording angels or every writer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.anchor: وما يحتمل أن تكون موصولة ومصدرية، والضمير في يسطرون عائد على الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the pen may mean its users, so “they write” refers to those people and their written pages or act of writing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالقلم أصحابه، فيكون الضمير في يسطرون لهم،

BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.claim: The surah is early Meccan except verses 17–33 and 48–50, and is commonly placed after al-ʿAlaq as the second revelation; despite ordering disputes it reflects the first revelation’s atmosphere.
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r1.anchor: السورة مكية مبكرة، إلا آيات (17: 33، 48: 50) فمدنية

BINTSHATI:v2p39/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r2.claim: Some say the surah, or most of it, was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah and Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r2.anchor: وذكر بعضهم في أسباب نزولها أنها أو معظمها "في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي وأبى جهل بن هشام المخزومي

BINTSHATI:v2p39/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r3.claim: A proposed connection to the preceding surah says the opening clears the Prophet of accusations of madness, praises his patience and character, and answers the disbelievers’ claims of poetry and magic.
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r3.anchor: فبدأ سبحانه وتعالى هذه السورة ببراءته مما كانوا ينسبونه إليه من الجنون

BINTSHATI:v2p39/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r4.claim: The author says this coherence argument assumes muṣḥaf order: al-Mulk was revealed far later, around the seventy-seventh surah, over seventy revelations after al-Qalam.
BINTSHATI:v2p39/r4.anchor: وفيه التفات إلى نسق هذا الترتيب، ولا يفوتنا معه أن سورة الملك نزلت متأخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r1.claim: The surah aims to reveal what was hidden and clarify what was obscure, identifying the rightly guided person through knowledge and acceptance of revelation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r2.claim: The guided person demonstrates guidance by acquiring knowledge, accepting the Qur’an, and embodying the Furqān and the qualities of the Merciful within human capacity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r2.anchor: حيازته العلم الذي هو النور الأعظم الذي لا يضل بمصاحبته بتقبل القرآن والتخلق بالفرقان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r3.claim: The names Nūn and al-Qalam signal the surah’s aim: Nūn’s encompassing form suggests comprehensive explanation, while the pen makes knowledge manifest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r3.anchor: كما يحيط ضوء الشمس بما يظهره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r4.claim: The basmalah describes God’s complete power and knowledge, creation’s blessing, and the completion of mercy for those guided to obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#s068/r4.anchor: الذي له الإحاطة الكاملة فهو على كل شيء قدير لأنه بكل شيء عليم

STUDYQURAN:68:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from the pen mentioned in its first verse.
STUDYQURAN:68:intro/r3.anchor: It takes its name from the mention of the pen in the first verse

TABATABAI:68:17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r3.claim: The disconnected letter Nun was discussed earlier in the interpretation of al-Shura.
TABATABAI:68:17/r3.anchor: تقدم الكلام في الحروف المقطعة التي في أوائل السور في تفسير سورة الشورى

TABATABAI:68:17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r4.claim: Qalam is the familiar pen; satar can mean a row of writing, planted trees, or people standing in a row, while the verb means writing line by line.
TABATABAI:68:17/r4.anchor: الصف من الكتابة، ومن الشجر المغروس ومن القوم الوقوف

TABATABAI:68:17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r5.claim: The oath concerns pen and writing in general, a great divine gift that preserves hidden events and meanings from the barriers of time and distance.
TABATABAI:68:17/r5.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن المراد بذلك مطلق القلم ومطلق ما يسطرون به وهو المكتوب

TABATABAI:68:17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:17/r6.claim: God taught speech and writing, as stated in 55:3–4 and 96:4–5; the oath honors a gift like other created blessings sworn by in the Quran.
TABATABAI:68:17/r6.anchor: وقد امتن الله سبحانه على الإنسان بهدايته إليهما وتعليمهما له

TABATABAI:68:17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:17/r7.claim: Other readings take ma as a verbal noun meaning writing, the pen as the highest pen and its writing as the angels' record, or the writing surface as the Preserved Tablet; the author regards these options as weak.
TABATABAI:68:17/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد بالقلم القلم الأعلى الذي في الحديث أنه أول ما خلق الله

TABATABAI:68:17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:17/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:17/r8.claim: Further options take the plural as honorific, or interpret pen and writing as writers and their written works; the author also calls these possibilities weak.
TABATABAI:68:17/r8.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون المراد ما يسطرون فيه وهو اللوح المحفوظ

TABATABAI:68:29-33/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r8.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r8.claim: A report explains Nun as a river in Paradise that God froze into ink; a luminous pen wrote in the luminous Preserved Tablet everything that was and will be until Resurrection.
TABATABAI:68:29-33/r8.anchor: عن سفيان بن سعيد الثوري عن الصادق عليه السلام في تفسير الحروف المقطعة في القرآن قال وأما ن فهو نهر في الجنة

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r1.speaker: سفيان
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r1.claim: Sufyan asks about the Tablet and Pen; the answer describes a chain of angelic intermediaries from the divine Throne through Gabriel to the prophets.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r1.anchor: قال سفيان فقلت له يا ابن رسول الله بين أمر اللوح والقلم والمداد فضل بيان

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r2.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says the Tablet and Pen are two angels.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم الكرخي قال سألت جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام عن اللوح والقلم قال هما ملكان

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r3.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r3.claim: ʿAli describes the Pen and Book as light in a guarded Tablet, witnessed by the angels brought near to God.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r3.anchor: عن الأصبغ بن نباتة عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام { ن والقلم وما يسطرون } القلم قلم من نور وكتاب من نور

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r4.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r4.claim: A report from al-Sadiq says the Pen was sealed and fell silent; the hidden Book is the source from which all copies are made.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r4.anchor: عن عبد الرحيم القصير عن الصادق عليه السلام في اللوح والقلم وفيه ثم ختم على فم القلم

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r5.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r5.claim: The Prophet describes a Tablet and Pen of light recording what will happen through the Day of Resurrection.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r5.anchor: قال لوح من نور وقلم من نور يجري بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r6.claim: The Pen's writing matches all events in reality, with nothing occurring contrary to what was written.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r6.anchor: أي منطبق على متن الكائنات من دون أن يتخلف شيء منها عما كتب هناك

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r7.claim: A parallel report says the Pen was sealed and would not speak again until the Day of Resurrection.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r7.anchor: ما في رواية أبي هريرة ثم ختم على في القلم فلم ينطق ولا ينطق إلى يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Quraysh insulted ʿAli after the Prophet honored him; the passage identifies the slanderers as those astray and ʿAli as among the guided.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال لما رأت قريش تقديم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا وإعظامه له نالوا من علي

THALABI:v10p243/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p243/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p243/r3.claim: The sequence after “Read” and al-Muddaththir was al-Qalam through “you are of great character,” then al-Ḍuḥā.
THALABI:v10p243/r3.anchor: ثم كان ما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن بعد اقرأ والمدثر، ن والقلم إلى قوله: وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم، ثم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r1.claim: Most tafsirs and Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī call the surah Sūrat Nūn wa-l-Qalam, following its opening words; al-Tirmidhī's collection is also cited.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r1.anchor: سميت هذه السورة في معظم التفاسير وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) { سورة ن والقلم على حكاية اللفظين الواقعين في أولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r2.claim: Some call it Sūrat Nūn, while some codices call it Sūrat al-Qalam; Ibn ʿĀshūr saw that name in a fifth-century Kufic manuscript.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r2.anchor: وفي بعض المصاحف سميت سورة القلم وكذلك رأيت تسميتها في مصحف مخطوط بالخط الكوفي في القرن الخامس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the surah is Meccan, with no disagreement among exegetes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r3.anchor: وهي مكية قال ابن عطية : لا خلاف في ذلك بين أهل التأويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r6.claim: Jābir ibn Zayd ranks it as the second surah revealed, after al-ʿAlaq and before al-Muzzammil and al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r6.anchor: وهذه السورة عدها جابر بن زيد ثانية السور نزولا قال : نزلت بعد سورة { اقرأ باسم ربك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r7.claim: He prefers ʿĀʾisha's report that al-ʿAlaq was first, followed by a pause and al-Muddaththir; he reconciles Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh by placing al-Muddaththir after al-ʿAlaq.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r7.anchor: والأصح حديث عائشة أن أول ما أنزل سورة اقرأ باسم ربك ثم فتر الوحي ثم نزلت سورة المدثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r8.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says most of the surah was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Abū Jahl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p57/r8.anchor: وفي تفسير القرطبي } : أن معظم السورة نزل في الوليد بن المغيرة وأبي جهل

TABRISI:68:1-16/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16/r7.claim: One view takes ن as the name of this surah, like Ha Mim and Sad, as discussed among the interpretations of the opening of al-Baqara.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r7.anchor: فقيل هو اسم من أسماء السورة مثل حم وص وما أشبه ذلك

TABRISI:68:1-16/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل والسدي
TABRISI:68:1-16/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muqatil, and al-Suddi say ن is the fish that bears the earths.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو الحوت الذي عليه الأرضون عن ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل والسدي

TABRISI:68:1-16/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:68:1-16/r9.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies ن as a letter from the name al-Rahman.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو حرف من حروف الرحمن في رواية أخرى عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:68:1-16/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
TABRISI:68:1-16/r10.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak say ن means an inkwell.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو الدواة عن الحسن وقتادة والضحاك

TABRISI:68:1-16/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:68:1-16/r11.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says ن is a tablet of light.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r11.anchor: وقيل: نون لوح من نور وروي مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:68:1-16/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:68:1-16/r12.claim: Abu Jaafar al-Baqir says ن is a river in Paradise that God turned into ink; it froze, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and the Pen wrote all past and future events until Resurrection.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r12.anchor: وكان أبيض من اللبن وأحلى من الشهد ثم قال: للقلم اكتب فكتب القلم ما كان وما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

TABRISI:68:1-16/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16/r13.claim: Another view takes it as a fish in the sea, a sign of God because it lives in water and dies outside it, as land animals die in water.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r13.anchor: وقيل: المراد به الحوت في البحر وهو من آيات الله إذ خلقها في الماء فإذا فارق الماء مات

TABRISI:68:1-16/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16/r14.claim: The Pen is the writing implement God swears by for its benefits: it is one of humanity's two tongues, conveying the heart's contents and communicating at a distance, preserving religious law and ordering the world.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r14.anchor: { والقلم } الذي يكتب به أقسم الله به لمنافع الخلق فيه إذ هو أحد لساني الإنسان يؤدي عنه ما في جنانه ويبلغ البعيد عنه ما يبلغ القريب بلسانه

TABRISI:68:1-16/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16/r15.claim: Spoken words fade over the years, while the statement of pens endures through the ages.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r15.anchor: بيان اللسان تدرسه الأعوام وبيان الأقلام باق على مر الأيام

TABRISI:68:1-16/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16/r16.claim: A poet says religion and worldly life rest on two things, the Pen and sword, with the sword subordinate to the Pen.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن قوام أمور الدين والدنيا بشيئين القلم والسيف والسيف تحت القلم

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r1.claim: The angels write revelation conveyed to them and record human deeds; the oath includes the pen and its writing.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r1.anchor: وما يكتبه الملائكة مما يوحي إليهم وما يكتبونه من أعمال بني آدم

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r2.claim: On the alternative مصدرية reading, the oath is by the pen and their act of writing.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r2.anchor: إن ما مصدرية وتقديره والقلم وسطرهم فيكون القسم بالكتابة

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r3.claim: On the first reading, the oath is by what is written.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r3.anchor: وعلى القول الأول يكون القسم بالمكتوب

TABRISI:68:1-16#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#4/r6.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم
TABRISI:68:1-16#4/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Quraysh maligned ʿAlī after seeing the Prophet honor him; revelation identifies the accusers as astray and ʿAlī as guided.
TABRISI:68:1-16#4/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم قال: لما رأت قريش تقديم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عليا

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، مقاتل، السدي
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Suddī report that Nūn means a fish, invoking Dhū al-Nūn as a Quranic parallel.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r1.anchor: وهذا القول مروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل والسدي

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r2.claim: Some proponents take the fish to be the whale on whose back the earth rests in a sea beneath the lowest earth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r2.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r3.claim: Others take it to be the whale that held Jonah in its belly.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r3.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي احتبس يونس عليه السلام في بطنه

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r4.claim: Another view identifies it as the whale that stained Nimrod’s arrow with its blood.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r4.anchor: منهم من قال : إنه قسم بالحوت الذي لطخ سهم نمروذ بدمه

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r5.speaker: الضحاك، الحسن، قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also transmitted, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda preferred, that Nūn means an inkwell; the poem uses nūn in that sense.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r5.anchor: واختيار الضحاك والحسن وقتادة أن النون هو الدواة

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r6.claim: If Nūn means an inkwell, the oath pairs inkwell and pen because writing is greatly useful: communication comes through speech or writing.

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r7.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r7.claim: A report raised to the Prophet identifies Nūn as a tablet on which angels write what God commands them.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r7.anchor: أن النون لوح تكتب الملائكة ما يأمرهم الله به فيه رواه معاوية بن قرة مرفوعا

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r8.claim: A further view takes Nūn as the ink with which the angels write.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r8.anchor: أن النون هو المداد الذي تكتب به الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r9.claim: The proposed oath interpretations are weak on case grounds: a generic fish or inkwell should be indefinite and genitive, while a proper name should be declinable and genitive or indeclinable with fatḥa.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r9.anchor: هذه الوجوه ضعيفة لأنا إذا جعلناه مقسما به وجب إن كان جنسا أن نجره وننونه

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r10.claim: A fifth view says Nūn is the final letter of al-Raḥmān and intends an oath by the whole name; Rāzī rejects it as opening the door to esoteric absurdities.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r10.anchor: وهذا أيضا ضعيف لأن تجويزه يفتح باب ترهات الباطنية

RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r11.claim: Rāzī holds that Nūn is either the sūra’s name, a challenge, or one of the other explanations discussed at the opening of al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v30p68/r11.anchor: بل الحق أنه إما أن يكون اسما للسورة أو يكون الغرض منه التحدي أو سائر الوجوه المذكورة في أول سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r1.claim: Readers differ over pronouncing the nūn distinctly or concealing it: pausing at the spelled letter requires clarity, while treating it as connected to the next word permits concealment.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r1.anchor: القراء مختلفون في إظهار النون وإخفائه

RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers distinct pronunciation because the letter is spelled out and spelled letters are treated like paused forms even when connected.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء : وإظهارها أعجب إلي لأنها هجاء

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.claim: One view takes the oath’s pen generically to mean every pen used in heaven and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r1.anchor: القسم به هو الجنس وهو واقع على كل قلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.claim: The generic pen recalls God’s gift of writing as well as speech: writing lets a person communicate with someone distant as speech does with someone present.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r2.anchor: ووجه الانتفاع به أن ينزل الغائب منزلة المخاطب

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.claim: A second view identifies the oath’s pen as the particular pen mentioned in the report that it was the first thing God created.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r3.anchor: أن المقسم به هو القلم المعهود الذي جاء في الخبر أن أول ما خلق الله القلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the pen, ordered it to record all events until the Hour, and it wrote lifespans and deeds; it is a pen of light spanning heaven and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أول ما خلق الله القلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the first-created pen wrote destiny through the Day of Resurrection, so people proceed according to a decree already completed.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r5.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال : أول ما خلق الله القلم

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.claim: The Qāḍī reads the pen report metaphorically: a writing tool cannot be a living, responsible being; rather, God’s power brings all events to pass without resistance, like “Be, and it is.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا الخبر يجب حمله على المجاز

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r7.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r7.claim: Some identify the pen with the intellect, the source of created things, and infer that it is one with the primordial jewel described in another report.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r7.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن القلم المذكور ههنا هو العقل

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r8.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r8.claim: Their second report says the first creation was a jewel; God regarded it with awe, it melted and heated, and smoke and foam arose, from which heaven and earth were made respectively.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r8.anchor: وفي خبر آخر : أول ما خلق الله تعالى جوهرة

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r9.claim: They combine the reports by identifying the pen, intellect, and primordial jewel as one thing, arguing that otherwise the reports would contradict each other.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#2/r9.anchor: فهذه الأخبار بمجموعها تدل على أن القلم والعقل وتلك الجوهرة التي هي أصل المخلوقات شيء واحد

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r1.claim: The phrase with mā can function as a verbal noun meaning their writing, or refer to what is written; either reading makes the writing or written material the object of the oath.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r1.anchor: ما مع ما بعدها في تقدير المصدر

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r2.claim: If the pen means all pens in creation, God swears by every pen and everything written by every pen.

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r3.claim: Another view takes what is written to be what the guardian angels and noble scribes record.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : بل المراد ما يسطره الحفظة والكرام الكاتبون

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r4.claim: The word “pen” may stand for its writers, making the pronoun in “they write” refer to pen-owners and their written records.

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r5.claim: If the pen is the particular primordial pen, “what they write” may mean the Preserved Tablet on which it writes; the plural is honorific, not literal.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r5.anchor: أي وما يسطرون فيه وهو اللوح المحفوظ

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means everything recorded on the Preserved Tablet: deeds, lifespans, and all events through the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r6.anchor: الأشياء التي سطرت فيه من الأعمال والأعمار

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r1.claim: Nūn is the Arabic letter n and a separated letter whose outward meaning is unspecified; many say its meaning is known only to God.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r1.anchor: whose meaning is not specified outwardly

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r2.claim: This is the earliest sūrah in revelation chronology in which separated letters appear.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r2.anchor: This is the earliest sūrah in the chronological order of revelation in which the separated letters appear.

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r3.claim: Nūn also means fish; some commentators connect it with an old Arab myth that Earth rests on a mythical fish's back.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r3.anchor: some commentators thus relate it to an old Arab myth

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r4.claim: Others take Nūn's cup-shaped Arabic form as an allusion to the inkwell from which the pen draws ink.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r4.anchor: others say it refers to the

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r5.claim: In Islamic metaphysics, the Pen symbolizes the Divine Intellect or Logos through which God brings all things into being.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r5.anchor: In Islamic metaphysics, the Pen is often taken as a symbol for the Divine Intellect or Logos, through which God brought all things into being.

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r6.claim: What the Pen writes signifies the existence of beings in creation, while Nūn represents the reservoir of possibilities manifested there.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r6.anchor: by the Pen then means existiation of beings in the created order

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r7.speaker: ḥadīth qudsī
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r7.claim: A famous hadith qudsi says God created the Pen first and commanded it to write the decree of all that would occur until the Hour; no grading is stated.

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r8.claim: Nūn may allude to Divine Names containing nūn: al-Raḥmān, al-Nūr, or al-Nāṣir.

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r9.speaker: Bg, Q
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r9.claim: Others connect Nūn with God's helping the believers, naṣr al-muʾminīn, a phrase appearing in 30:47.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r9.anchor: Others see it as a reference to God’s helping the believers (naṣr al-muʾminīn; Bg, Q)

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r10.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r10.claim: Some attribute to the Prophet the saying that Nūn is a tablet of light; no grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r10.anchor: Some attribute to the Prophet the saying

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r11.speaker: Bg, IK, JJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r11.claim: The pronoun they in that which they inscribe may refer to angels who record all human deeds; related passages include 43:80, 50:17–18, 80:15–16, 82:10–12, and 86:4.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r11.anchor: The pronoun they in that which they inscribe may be seen as a reference to the angels who record all human deeds

STUDYQURAN:68:1/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r12.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r12.claim: Al-Qurṭubī divides pens into those recording the decree until Resurrection, angels' pens recording human deeds, and human writing pens; he cites 18:49 for the second kind.
STUDYQURAN:68:1/r12.anchor: According to al-Qurṭubī, pens are of three principal types

TAB-FULL:v23p141/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r1.claim: In reports from Ibn ʿAbbās, Nūn is the whale supporting the earth: after the pen and heavens are created, the earth rests on the whale, whose movement makes it quake until mountains steady it.
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «أول ما خلق الله من شيء القلم، فجرى بما هو كائن، ثم رفع بخار الماء، فخلقت منه السموات، ثم خلق النون فبسطت الأرض على ظهر النون

TAB-FULL:v23p141/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r2.claim: Mujāhid says Nūn was said to be the whale beneath the seventh earth.
TAB-FULL:v23p141/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: كان يقال النون: الحوت الذي تحت الأرض السابعة

TAB-FULL:v23p142/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the pen was created first and wrote what would happen until the Hour; then Nūn was created above water and the earth packed upon it.
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: إن أول شيء خلق ربي القلم، فقال له: اكتب، فكتب ما هو كائن إلى أن تقوم الساعة، ثم خلق النون فوق الماء

TAB-FULL:v23p142/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says alif-lām-rā, ḥā-mīm, and Nūn are disjoint letters belonging to the name al-Raḥmān.
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r2.anchor: عن يزيد، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: الر، وحم، ون حروف الرحمن مقطعة

TAB-FULL:v23p142/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r3.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr calls the opening letters a segmented name.
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، قوله الر، وحم، ون. قال: اسم مقطع

TAB-FULL:v23p142/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies Nūn as the inkwell and says the pen recorded deeds and allotted provision; angels copied each day’s deeds from the heavenly storehouse.
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r4.anchor: عن ثابت البناني، عن ابن عباس، قال: إن الله خلق النون وهي الدواة، وخلق القلم، فقال: اكتب

TAB-FULL:v23p142/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās appeals to 45:29, “We used to copy what you did,” to argue that angelic transcription comes from an original record.
TAB-FULL:v23p142/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ألستم قوما عربا تسمعون الحفظة يقولون: {إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون} [الجاثية: 29] وهل يكون الاستنساخ إلا من أصل؟

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify Nūn as the inkwell.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r1.anchor: عن معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة، في قوله: {ن} [القلم: 1] قال: هو الدواة

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet describes Nūn as a tablet of light that records what will occur until the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r2.anchor: عن معاوية بن قرة، عن أبيه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] «لوح من نور يجري بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r3.claim: Qatāda says God swears by whatever He wills with the opening oath.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] يقسم الله بما شاء

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd also calls this an oath by God.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله: {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] قال: هذا قسم أقسم الله به

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r5.claim: Another reported view takes Nūn as the name of the sūra.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي اسم من أسماء السورة

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r6.claim: Another reported view takes Nūn as a letter of the alphabet, like the opening letters of other sūras.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي حرف من حروف المعجم؛ وقد ذكرنا القول فيما جانس ذلك من حروف الهجاء

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r7.speaker: عامة قراء الكوفة وعامة قراء البصرة
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r7.claim: Most Kufan readers except al-Kisāʾī and most Basrans pronounce the final nūn clearly, treating it as a letter name that takes a pause even when connected.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r7.anchor: فأظهر النون فيها وفي يس عامة قراء الكوفة خلا الكسائي، وعامة قراء البصرة، لأنها حرف هجاء، والهجاء مبني على الوقوف عليه وإن اتصل

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r8.speaker: الكسائي
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī assimilates and hides the final nūn, treating it as connected to what follows.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r8.anchor: وكان الكسائي يدغم النون الآخرة منهما ويخفيها بناء على الاتصال

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts both readings as eloquent but prefers clear pronunciation as more eloquent and more common.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r9.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا أنهما قراءتان فصيحتان بأيتهما قرأ القارئ أصاب، غير أن إظهار النون أفصح وأشهر، فهو أعجب إلي

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r10.claim: The pen is the familiar pen, specifically the one God created and commanded to write all that would occur until the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r10.anchor: وأما القلم: فهو القلم المعروف، غير أن الذي أقسم به ربنا من الأقلام: القلم الذي خلقه الله تعالى ذكره، فأمره فجرى بكتابة جميع ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v23p144/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r11.claim: The Prophet says the first thing God created was the pen, which He commanded to write destiny; it recorded what was and will be forever.
TAB-FULL:v23p144/r11.anchor: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن أول ما خلق الله خلق القلم، فقال له: اكتب، قال: يا رب وما أكتب؟ قال: اكتب القدر

TAB-FULL:v23p148/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says the first thing God created was the pen and He ordered it to write everything.
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، أنه كان يحدث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أول شيء خلق الله القلم وأمره فكتب كل شيء»

TAB-FULL:v23p148/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās argues that denial of predestination denies God’s Book: the pen recorded events through the Resurrection, so people act according to a decree already completed.
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: قلت لابن عباس: إن ناسا يكذبون بالقدر، فقال: إنهم يكذبون بكتاب الله

TAB-FULL:v23p148/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r3.claim: Mujāhid reports hearing ʿAbd Allāh, uncertain whether Ibn ʿUmar or Ibn ʿAbbās, say the pen wrote all that would be and people now act within what is finished.
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r3.anchor: قال: سمعت عبد الله لا ندري ابن عمر أو ابن عباس قال: إن أول ما خلق الله القلم، فجرى القلم بما هو كائن

TAB-FULL:v23p148/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r4.claim: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit reports the Prophet saying God first created the pen and it recorded what would happen until the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r4.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن أول ما خلق الله القلم، فقال له: اكتب فجرى في تلك الساعة

TAB-FULL:v23p148/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies the pen in the oath as the instrument by which the Reminder was written.
TAB-FULL:v23p148/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ن والقلم} [القلم: 1] قال: الذي كتب به الذكر

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r1.claim: The phrase means what people draw and write; on this reading the oath is by creation and their actions.
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] قال: وما يخطون

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, mā can be a verbal noun: “their writing what they write,” making the oath by the book.
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r2.anchor: كأنه قيل: ن والقلم والكتاب. وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل.

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as what people write or draw.
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] قال: وما يخطون

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as “they write.”
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] يقول: يكتبون

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as what they write.
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {وما يسطرون} [القلم: 1] قال: وما يكتبون

TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r6.claim: Sata ra is used for writing a book; al-Ṭabarī cites Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj’s verse as evidence for this usage.
TAB-FULL:v23p148#2/r6.anchor: ومنه قول رؤبة بن العجاج: [البحر الرجز] إني وأسطار سطرن سطرا

TAB-FULL:v1p15/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r1.speaker: أبو ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r1.claim: Abū Maysarah says the Qur’an contains words from every language.
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r1.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة، قال: «في القرآن من كل لسان

TAB-FULL:v1p15/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says this does not mean shared words were unknown or non-Arabic to Arabs; languages can use the same words with the same meanings, as with dirham, dinar, inkwell, pen, and paper.
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r2.anchor: كالدرهم، والدينار، والدواة، والقلم، والقرطاس وغير ذلك مما يتعب إحصاؤه

TAB-FULL:v1p15/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r3.claim: No one can establish which language originated a shared term without decisive knowledge-bearing evidence; neither Arabs nor other peoples have priority merely from common use.
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r3.anchor: لأن العرب ليست بأولى أن تكون كان مخرج أصل ذلك منها إلى العجم، ولا العجم بأحق

TAB-FULL:v1p15/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī’s preferred wording calls such terms Arabic-Ajamic or Ethiopic-Arabic, since both peoples use them as ordinary parts of their speech.
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r4.anchor: بل الصواب في ذلك عندنا أن يسمى عربيا أعجميا، أو حبشيا عربيا

TAB-FULL:v1p15/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r5.claim: Affirming that a word belongs to one language does not deny its belonging to another when both use it; only mutually exclusive claims, like standing versus sitting, entail denial.
TAB-FULL:v1p15/r5.anchor: فأما ما جاز اجتماعه، فهو خارج من المعنى، وذلك كقول القائل: فلان قائم مكلم فلانا

BURSEVI:v10p78/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r1.speaker: بعض مفسران
BURSEVI:v10p78/r1.claim: A report in Kashf al-Asrar says a fish beneath the seven earths bore the earth like the letter Nun; when it feared and moved, Gabriel struck it, and it kept silent lest the earth be forgotten or shaken at Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r1.anchor: في كشف الأسرار) : بعض مفسران كفتند ماهيت برآب زير هفت طبقه زمين

BURSEVI:v10p78/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p78/r2.claim: The fish’s burden earned two honors: God swore by it, and it was spared slaughter; the lesson is that one who bears a burden is not left unrewarded, and a believer bearing the divine trust is spared separation.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r2.anchor: دو تشريف داديكى آنكه بد وقسم ياد كرد محل قسم خداوند جهان كشت ديكر تشريف آنست كه كارد از حلق او برداشت

BURSEVI:v10p78/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p78/r3.claim: The قلم is the instrument used for writing; the waw is an oath under the first grammatical construction and a conjunction under the second.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r3.anchor: هو ما يكتب به والواو وللقسم على التقدير الأول وللعطف على الثاني

BURSEVI:v10p78/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p78/r4.claim: The intended pen is the Pen of the Preserved Tablet.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r4.anchor: والمراد قلم اللوح كما جاء في الخبران أول ما خلق الله القلم

BURSEVI:v10p78/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r5.speaker: الخبر
BURSEVI:v10p78/r5.claim: A transmitted account says the first created thing was the Pen: God told it to write what would occur through Judgment Day, and it recorded lifespans, deeds, and provisions on the Preserved Tablet; it was then sealed until Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r5.anchor: كما جاء في الخبران أول ما خلق الله القلم ونظر إليه فانشق بنصفين ثم قال له أجر بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v10p78/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p78/r6.claim: The record of destiny on the Preserved Tablet is the decree that must be believed in, in both its good and evil.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r6.anchor: فجرى على اللوح المحفوظ بذلك من الآجال والأعمال والأرزاق وهو القدر الذي يجب أن يؤمن بخيره وشره

BURSEVI:v10p78/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p78/r7.claim: In the account’s cosmology, after the Pen God created Nun, the fish; the earth was spread over it, water vapor rose and formed the heavens, and mountains anchored the earth when the fish moved it.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r7.anchor: وبعدما خلق القلم خلق النون أي السمكة فدحا الأرض عليها فارتفع بخار الماء ففتق منه السموات

BURSEVI:v10p78/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p78/r8.speaker: الواحدي
BURSEVI:v10p78/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi’s account says God first created the Pen, then Nun as the inkwell, and the Pen wrote from that inkwell all that was and would be; the oath is by the luminous inkwell and Pen.
BURSEVI:v10p78/r8.anchor: وفي رواية الواحدي في الوسيط أول يزى كه خداي تعالى بيا فريد قلم بود س نون را بيا فريدو آن دو اتست

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r1.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with its relative clause pronoun omitted; السطر can mean a row of writing, planted trees, or people standing, and سطر فلان means he wrote.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r1.anchor: ما موصولة والعائد محذوف والسطر الصف من الكتابة ومن الشجر المغروس ومن القوم الوقوف وسطر فلان كذا أي كتبه

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r2.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the people of the Pen, inferred from mention of the Pen; the clause means what they write.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r2.anchor: القلم المدلول عليه بذكره والمعنى بالفارسية وديكر سوكند ياد فرمود

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r3.speaker: ابن هيضم
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r3.claim: A report in al-Tibyan from Ibn Haytham interprets Nun as the inkpot, the Pen as the tongue, and what is written as the guardian angels’ record of a servant’s deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r3.anchor: درتبيان از ابن هيضم رحمه الله ، نقل فرمودكه

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r4.claim: Some gnostics read Nun as the Essence, the Pen as the divine attributes, and the writing as divine acts and affairs inscribed letter by letter on the Tablet of Power and Will.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r4.anchor: قال بعض العارفين النون نون الذات والقلم قلم الصفات وما يسطرون هي الأفعال والشؤون الإلهية

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r5.claim: Bursevi reads Nun as the inkpot of collective essential unity and the source of the existent Book, gathering the ink and materials of the world’s forms; alternatively it is the point marking the level of absolute oneness.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r5.anchor: يقول الفقير فيه إشارة إلى أن نون الجمع الذاتي أي دواته وهو أصل كتاب الوجود الذي هو أم الكتاب

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r6.speaker: الإمام علي
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r6.claim: Imam Ali is quoted as saying in a public sermon that he is the point beneath the ب of Bismillah, the Pen, the Preserved Tablet, the Throne, the Footstool, the seven heavens, and the earths; afterward he professed servanthood and subjection to divine decrees.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r6.anchor: وقد كان الإمام على رضي الله عنه يقول في خطبته على رؤوس الإشهاد إنا نقطة باء بسم الله

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r7.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya reads Nun as undifferentiated knowledge within essential oneness and the Pen as detailed knowledge in the unity of names; the inkwell contains every letter and word as a seed contains its tree, and the Pen inscribes that implicit knowledge onto the heart’s tablet in detail.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r7.anchor: التأويلات النجمية : يشير بكلمة ن إلى العلم الإجمالي المندمج

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r8.claim: Bursevi says God swears by His general knowledge in essential oneness and detailed knowledge in named unity, ultimately by absolute oneness of Essence and the collective unity of Names, since knowledge is identical with Essence, and by all the divine letters and words inscribed by the Pen.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r8.anchor: فإذا فهمت المقصود فاعلم إن الله تعالى اقسم بعلمه الأجمالي الكائن في الأحدية وبعلمه التفصيلي الثابت في الواحدية

BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r9.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r9.claim: Some great masters map the shadowy Book of Existence as hidden affairs for letters, fixed entities for words, spiritual and imaginal realities for verses, and sensible forms for complete suras; the real Book consists of essential, attribute, and action names and their manifestations.
BURSEVI:v10p79#2/r9.anchor: كما قال بعض الكبار في بيان حروف كتاب الوجود الظلي وكلماته وآياته وسوره إن الشؤون الغيبة حروفه العاليات

THALABI:v10p5#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r1.speaker: بعض القراء
THALABI:v10p5#3/r1.claim: Some readers pronounce the nūn of ن clearly and others conceal it.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r1.anchor: ن اختلف القراء فيه، فأظهر بعضهم نونه، وأخفاها الآخرون

THALABI:v10p5#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p5#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reads ن with kasra, assuming an omitted oath particle.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس (ن) بكسر النون على إضمار حرف القسم

THALABI:v10p5#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
THALABI:v10p5#3/r3.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads ن with fatḥa, assuming an omitted verb.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بالفتح على إضمار فعل

THALABI:v10p5#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل ومرة الهمداني وعطاء الخراساني والسدي والكلبي
THALABI:v10p5#3/r4.claim: These interpreters say ن is the fish that carries the earth.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r4.anchor: فقال مجاهد ومقاتل ومرة الهمداني وعطاء الخراساني والسدي والكلبي: هو الحوت الذي يحمل الأرض

THALABI:v10p5#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p5#3/r5.claim: In the report transmitted by Abu Zabyan, the pen first writes all that will be; water and the heavens are created, then Nun spreads the earth on its back, and mountains stabilize the moving earth.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r5.anchor: وهي رواية أبي ظبيان عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم فجرى بما هو كائن، ثم رفع فخلق الماء فخلق منه السماوات

THALABI:v10p5#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r6.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v10p5#3/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil give the fish's name as Yamhut.

THALABI:v10p5#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r7.speaker: أبو اليقظان والواقدي وأبو كعب
THALABI:v10p5#3/r7.claim: Abu al-Yaqzan, al-Waqidi and Abu Kab call the fish Lusa.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r7.anchor: وقال أبو اليقظان والواقدي وأبو كعب: لوسا

THALABI:v10p5#3/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r8.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب
THALABI:v10p5#3/r8.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib gives the fish's name as Yalhut.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r8.anchor: وقال علي ابن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: يلهوت

THALABI:v10p5#3/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r9.speaker: الراجز
THALABI:v10p5#3/r9.claim: The rajaz poet uses يلهوت as the fish's name, witnessing the form attached to that interpretation of ن.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r9.anchor: وقال الراجز. ما لي أراكم كلكم سكوتا … والله ربي خالق اليلهوتا

THALABI:v10p5#3/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p5#3/r10.speaker: الرواة
THALABI:v10p5#3/r10.claim: The narrators give a cosmology in which an angel bears the seven earths, a bull supports him on a ruby, a green rock supports the bull, and a giant fish supports the rock; wind rests on divine power, and God commands it to be.
THALABI:v10p5#3/r10.anchor: قالت الرواة: لما خلق الله تعالى الأرض وفتقها بعث الله سبحانه من تحت العرش ملكا، فهبط إلى الأرض حتى دخل تحت الأرضين السبع

THALABI:v10p6/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v10p6/r1.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says Satan whispered to the fish bearing the earth that it could shake off all creatures; God sent a creature into its nostril and brain, and the fish's distress was relieved, with the creature to return if it tries again.
THALABI:v10p6/r1.anchor: وقال كعب الأحبار: إن إبليس تغلغل إلى الحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض كلها فوسوس إليه

THALABI:v10p6/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r2.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p6/r2.claim: A report from Ikrima through Ibn Abbas says ن represents the final letter of the name al-Rahman, alongside الر and حم.
THALABI:v10p6/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هي آخر حروف الرحمن، وهي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: الر وحم ون

THALABI:v10p6/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
THALABI:v10p6/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak interpret ن as an inkpot; Thabit al-Yamani transmits this from Ibn Abbas.
THALABI:v10p6/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة والضحاك: النون: الدواة، وهي رواية ثابت اليماني عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p6/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r4.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v10p6/r4.claim: The cited poet uses النون for an inkpot, which casts streaming tears when longing drives him toward his beloved.
THALABI:v10p6/r4.anchor: وقال فيه الشاعر: إذا ما الشوق يرح بي إليهم … ألقت النون بالدمع السجوم

THALABI:v10p6/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r5.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
THALABI:v10p6/r5.claim: Muawiya ibn Qurra identifies ن as a tablet of light and raises this report to the Prophet.
THALABI:v10p6/r5.anchor: وقال معاوية بن قرة: هو لوح من نور، ورفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v10p6/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p6/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says ن is an object by which God swears.
THALABI:v10p6/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو قسم أقسم الله تعالى به

THALABI:v10p6/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r7.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p6/r7.claim: Ibn Kaysan calls ن the opening of the surah.

THALABI:v10p6/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r8.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p6/r8.claim: Ata interprets ن as an opening drawn from the divine names Nur, Nasir and Nasir.
THALABI:v10p6/r8.anchor: عطاء: افتتاح اسمه نور وناصر ونصير

THALABI:v10p6/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r9.speaker: القرظي
THALABI:v10p6/r9.claim: Al-Qurazi says God swears by His support of believers, as shown by the promise that aiding believers is incumbent upon Him.
THALABI:v10p6/r9.anchor: [القرظي] : أقسم الله تعالى بنصرته المؤمنين بيانه قوله: كان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

THALABI:v10p6/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r10.speaker: جعفر الصادق
THALABI:v10p6/r10.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq says ن is a river in Paradise.
THALABI:v10p6/r10.anchor: جعفر الصادق: هو نهر في الجنة

THALABI:v10p6/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p6/r11.claim: The Pen is the one with which the Remembrance was written, a pen of light spanning between heaven and earth.
THALABI:v10p6/r11.anchor: والقلم وهو الذي كتب به الذكر، وهو قلم من نور ما بين السماء والأرض

THALABI:v10p6/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r12.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
THALABI:v10p6/r12.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports that the first created thing was the Pen, commanded to write knowledge and all that would exist forever; his deathbed counsel also affirms belief in divine decree, good and bad.
THALABI:v10p6/r12.anchor: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إن أول ما خلق الله القلم فقال له: اكتب، فقال: يا رب وما أكتب؟ فقال: اكتب العلم

THALABI:v10p6/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p6/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p6/r13.claim: A report says God first created the Pen, split it in two, then commanded it to write everything destined until Resurrection on the Preserved Tablet.
THALABI:v10p6/r13.anchor: ويقال: لما خلق الله تعالى القلم وهو أول ما خلقه نظر إليه فانشق نصفين، ثم قال: اجر، فقال: يا رب بم أجري

THALABI:v10p7/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r1.speaker: ابن الزيات
THALABI:v10p7/r1.claim: An anecdote says Ibn al-Zayyat comforted a grieving caliph with verses invoking divine favor, the dominance of decree and what was written on the Tablet.
THALABI:v10p7/r1.anchor: وحكي أن ابن الزيات دخل على بعض الخلفاء فوجده مغموما، وقال له: روح عني يا ابن الزيات

THALABI:v10p7/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p7/r2.claim: The Pen may mean the writing instrument and writing that God graciously taught human beings, as in the verse about teaching by the Pen.
THALABI:v10p7/r2.anchor: وهل أراد بالقلم الخط والكتابة الذي امتن الله تعالى على عباده بتعليمه إياهم؟ ذلك كما قال: علم بالقلم

THALABI:v10p7/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r3.speaker: ابن هيثم
THALABI:v10p7/r3.claim: Ibn Haytham says the Pen's dignity lies in the fact that no book for God was written except by it, which explains the oath by it.
THALABI:v10p7/r3.anchor: فقال ابن هيثم: من جلالة القلم أنه لم يكتب لله تعالى كتاب إلا به لذلك أقسم الله تعالى به

THALABI:v10p7/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r4.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p7/r4.claim: An anonymous saying calls pens mounts for intelligence and messengers for the noble.
THALABI:v10p7/r4.anchor: وقيل: الأقلام مطايا الفطن ورسل الكرام

THALABI:v10p7/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r5.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p7/r5.claim: Another saying calls the Pen the greatest ظلم, a striking but unexplained characterization in the text.

THALABI:v10p7/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p7/r6.claim: The passage distinguishes expression by tongue from expression by fingers: writing endures through the ages while spoken expression is worn away.
THALABI:v10p7/r6.anchor: وقيل: البيان اثنان: بيان لسان وبيان بنان، وفضل بيان البنان أن ما تثبته الأقلام باق على الأيام

THALABI:v10p7/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r7.speaker: بعض الحكماء
THALABI:v10p7/r7.claim: Some sages say worldly and religious affairs rest on the Pen and sword, with the sword subordinate to knowledge.
THALABI:v10p7/r7.anchor: وقال بعض الحكماء: قوام أمور الدين والدنيا شيئان: القلم والسيف، والسيف تحت العلم

THALABI:v10p7/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r8.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p7/r8.claim: The accompanying poem depicts the sword as serving the Pen and following what the Pen writes.
THALABI:v10p7/r8.anchor: إن يخدم القلم السيف الذي خضعت … له الرقاب ودانت دون حذره الأمم

THALABI:v10p7/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r9.speaker: الصنوبري
THALABI:v10p7/r9.claim: Al-Sunawbari compares a weak, hollow reed Pen to a lance, arrows, a polished sword and a lion, claiming its force and courage surpass them.
THALABI:v10p7/r9.anchor: وللصنوبري: قلم من القصب الضعيف الأجوف … أمضى من الرمح الطويل الأثيف

THALABI:v10p7/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r10.speaker: أبو تمام
THALABI:v10p7/r10.claim: Abu Tammam says a writer's stroke in eloquence is sharper and more forceful than a polished sword, and pens can spill blood through their points.
THALABI:v10p7/r10.anchor: قال: أنشدني ابن صفون لأبي تمام في معناه: ولضربة من كاتب في بيانه … أمضى وأبلغ من رقيق حسام

THALABI:v10p7/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r11.speaker: البحتري
THALABI:v10p7/r11.claim: Al-Buhturi says people can use pens to defeat numerous enemies in ways swords cannot reach.
THALABI:v10p7/r11.anchor: وللبحتري: قوم إذا أجدوا الأقلام عن غضب … ثم استمدوا بها ماء المنيات

THALABI:v10p7/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p7/r12.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p7/r12.claim: Another poet says a Pen is more effective in adversity than a sword that shines in anger.
THALABI:v10p7/r12.anchor: وقال آخر: ما السيف غضبا يضيء رونقه … أمضى على النائبات من قلمه

THALABI:v10p8/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r1.speaker: ابن الرومي
THALABI:v10p8/r1.claim: Ibn al-Rumi says the Pen erases and confirms people's livelihoods, so decrees are only what it erases and writes.
THALABI:v10p8/r1.anchor: ولأبن الرومي: في كفه قلم ناهيك من قلم … نبلا وناهيك من كف به اتشحا

THALABI:v10p8/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r2.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v10p8/r2.claim: An anonymous poem portrays the Pen as a mute object that speaks authoritative words through its silent, hollow body.
THALABI:v10p8/r2.anchor: قال: وأنشد بعضهم في وصفه: وأخرس ينطق بالمحكمات … وجثمانه صامت أجوف

THALABI:v10p8/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r3.speaker: آخر
THALABI:v10p8/r3.claim: Another poem describes the reed Pen's worn tip, its writing in darkness and its ability to make the reader understand unheard speech.
THALABI:v10p8/r3.anchor: والآخر في وصفه: نحف الشوى بعد ما على أم رأسه … ويحفى ويقوى عدوه حين يقطع

THALABI:v10p8/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r4.speaker: آخر
THALABI:v10p8/r4.claim: A further poem compares the Pen's trimmed reed to trees and evokes tears and black ink as it writes.
THALABI:v10p8/r4.anchor: اخذه وما شجرات نابتات بفقره … إذا قطعت حارت مطايا الأصابع

THALABI:v10p8/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p8/r5.claim: يسطرون means “they write”; alternatively, the phrase means “and those who write them,” namely the scribes.
THALABI:v10p8/r5.anchor: قوله: وما يسطرون يكتبون، ويجوز أن يكون معناه ويسطرهم يعني السفرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r1.claim: Mujāhid, Muqātil, and al-Suddī identify nūn as the whale carrying the earth in a sea beneath the lowest earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r1.anchor: وقول مجاهد ومقاتل والسدي (¬2)، قالوا: هو الحوت الذي يحمل الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r2.claim: In Arabic, nūn means fish; the Qurʾān uses it in Jonah’s epithet Dhū al-Nūn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r2.anchor: والنون في اللغة السمكة (¬4). ومنه قوله تعالى في ذكر يونس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that nūn means an inkpot; al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda also hold this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r3.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: (ن) الدواة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r4.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r4.claim: A poetic line uses nūn to mean inkpot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر (¬4): إذا ما الشوق برح بي إليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r5.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r5.claim: ʿIkrima reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that nūn is the final letter of al-Raḥmān; alif-lām-rā, ḥā-mīm, and nūn are disjointed letters of that name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r5.anchor: وروى عكرمة (¬5) عن ابن عباس أن نون هاهنا آخر حروف الرحمن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r6.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r6.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says nūn here is a tablet of light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r6.anchor: وروى معاوية بن قرة (¬7) مرفوعا أن نون هاهنا لوح من نور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Kaysān say nūn is a surah-opening letter like the other disjointed openings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة وابن كيسان (¬1): نون فاتحة السورة كسائر الفواتح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r8.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad says nūn is the name of an alphabet letter like qāf and mīm; this is likelier because a fish-name would decline, whereas alphabet names are paused.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r8.anchor: وقال المبرد: (ن) اسم الحرف المعروف من حروف الهجاء نحو (ق) و (م). وهذا هو الأشبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r9.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad favors interpreting nūn as an alphabet opener, specifically the final letter of al-Raḥmān, since it is built on a vowelless pause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r9.anchor: وقال المبرد: (ن) اسم الحرف المعروف من حروف الهجاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r10.speaker: القراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r10.claim: Readers differ on pronouncing nūn clearly or assimilating it before “by the pen”; clear pronunciation treats it as paused, while concealment treats it as connected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r10.anchor: والقراء مختلفون في إظهار النون وإخفائه من قوله {ن * والقلم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r11.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers clear pronunciation because the letter is spelled out, and spelled letters are like pauses even when connected.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: وإظهارها أعجب إلي، لأنها هجاء، والهجاء كالوقوف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r12.claim: The author refers to his discussion of the same pronunciation issue at 38:1 and 36:1–2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p69#3/r12.anchor: وقد ذكرنا هذا في قوله: {ص * والقرآن}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first thing God created was the pen, which He commanded to write everything that would happen until the Hour; it is a pen of light as long as the distance between heaven and earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أول ما خلق الله القلم ثم قال له: اكتب ما هو كائن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r2.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r2.claim: Mujāhid reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that God first created the pen and commanded it to write destiny through the Resurrection; people follow a decree already completed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r2.anchor: وروى مجاهد عنه قال: كان أول (¬2) ما خلق الله القلم فقال له: اكتب القدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r3.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r3.claim: All exegetes identify the pen as the one that wrote the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r3.anchor: وهذا قول جميع المفسرين. قالوا: هو القلم الذي كتب به اللوح المحفوظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p72/r4.claim: Exegetes say “what they write” refers to the recording angels’ records of human deeds.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r1.claim: The letter nūn refers to the whale on whose back the earth rests.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r1.anchor: أقسم بالحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r2.claim: The Pen is the one God created to write what will occur through the Day of Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r2.anchor: القلم الذي خلقه الله تعالى، فجرى بالكائنات إلى يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r3.claim: Those who write are the angels.

QASHANI:68:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r1.claim: The letter Nun signifies the Universal Soul.

QASHANI:68:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r2.claim: The Pen signifies the Universal Intellect, whose influence inscribes forms of beings into the Soul as a pen inscribes on a tablet.
QASHANI:68:1/r2.anchor: تنتقش في النفس صور الموجودات بتأثير العقل كما تنتقش الصور في اللوح بالقلم

QASHANI:68:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r3.claim: Nun is an allusion that gives only the first letter of a word; the Pen is a simile.
QASHANI:68:1/r3.anchor: والأول من باب الكناية بالاكتفاء من الكلمة بأول حروفها

QASHANI:68:1/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r4.claim: What they write comprises forms, essences, and states of things decreed to occur.
QASHANI:68:1/r4.anchor: من صور الأشياء وماهياتها وأحوالها المقدرة على ما يقع عليها

QASHANI:68:1/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r5.claim: The writers are intermediary intellects and holy spirits, though God is the true writer and they are credited figuratively in the realm of the Divine Names.
QASHANI:68:1/r5.anchor: وفاعل ما يسطرون الكتبة من العقول المتوسطة والأرواح القدسة

QASHANI:68:1/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:1/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:1/r6.claim: The oath honors the Soul, Intellect, and their emanations as beginnings of existence and divine ordination, encompassing all being at the first level of influence and reception and fitting the subject sworn by.
QASHANI:68:1/r6.anchor: أقسم بهما وبما يصدر عنهما من مبادىء الوجود وصور التقدير الإلهي ومبدأ أمره

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r1.claim: At pause Nūn has sukūn; in connected recitation most readers pronounce it with izhār, while some assimilate it into wāw with or without ghunna.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r1.anchor: Nûn vakf üzere sâkindir. Vasıl hâlinde kıraatlerin ekserîsinde izhar ile, bazısında vâv’da gunneli veya gunnesiz idgam ile okunur.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r2.claim: Like the opening Ṭā Hā, Nūn is semantically among the ambiguous passages, though not lexically so for the author; outwardly it is the familiar letter nūn.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r2.anchor: bizim için lügaten olmasa bile mânen müteşâbihâttandır. Bunun zâhiri ص,ق gibi hurûf-i hecâdan bildiğimiz nûn harfi olmasıdır

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r3.claim: The letter’s dotted, circular form resembles an inkpot and its name begins and ends with the same sound; it is also among the most resonant speech sounds.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r3.anchor: Bir nokta ile bir hokka ve çanak gibi dâirevî bir şekilde yazılır. İsmi de evvel ve âhiri bir olan نُون lâfzıdır. Harf denilen sesler içinde en ihtizazlı bir ses olması

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r4.claim: Nūn can point from the ordered components of creation to God, just as words and sentences are assembled from letters; as a specific letter it can also indicate the alphabet generally.
