ELMALILI:68:1-6/r4.anchor: kitâb-ı fıtratın nizâmında derece derece müfredât ve besâitten mürekkebât dizilerek mebde’den müntehâya vücûd-i Hakk’a delâlet

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r5.claim: Other possible allusions are the human groan and cosmic resonance, the earth-and-sky world viewed as a hemisphere, or the letter’s resemblance to an inkwell and ink.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r5.anchor: enîn-i beşerin ve tanîn-i hilkatin en ziyade mümessili olan bir ses, yahut nazarımızda bir merkeze nâzır nısf-ı küre şeklinde tecellî eden âlemin Arz ve semâsıyla

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r6.claim: By pointing to the origins and purpose of speech and writing, Nūn’s oath draws attention to the value of language, writing, and the people of the pen, and issues a challenge.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r6.anchor: fıtratta kelâm ve yazının menşe’ ve gayesine telvih ve bunlara kasem ile lisânın ve yazının ve ehl-i kalemin kıymetine tenbih ederek tahaddî daveti ifade eder bir harftir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r7.claim: Nūn takes the mind from one point into the depths, inviting reflection on the letters of the revealed Book, the Book of creation, and the origin of existence.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r7.anchor: derinlere götürerek kitâb-ı münzelden kitâb-ı hilkate ve mebde’-i vücûda kadar bütün harfleri düşündürebilir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r8.claim: This reading of Nūn does not prevent the sūra from also taking its name from it.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r8.anchor: Ve böyle olması aynı zamanda sûrenin ismi olmasına da mâni‘değildir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r9.claim: Writing the symbol ن and reading it as Nūn signals that the letter itself, not its name, is intended; it is left uninflected and read at pause.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r9.anchor: müsemmâsı maksud olduğuna tenbih için ن yazılmış ve i‘rab olunmayıp vakf üzere okunmuştur.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r10.claim: The pause evokes the lament of those who lost the flowing water at the previous sūra’s end; only the Quran descending from the Merciful can soothe them, and pens should serve it.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r10.anchor: evvelki sûrenin âhirindeki mâ’-i ma‘îni kaybetmiş olanların enînleri ancak bir âb-ı revân gibi mâye-i hayat olmak üzere taraf-ı Rahmân’dan nâzil olan Kur’an ile dinlendirebileceğine

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r11.claim: Whatever else is intended, the apparent first meaning is the familiar letter nūn, which many exegetes also prefer; this partly resolves verbal ambiguity while semantic ambiguity remains.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r11.anchor: ن mâlumumuz bulunan nûn harfi olmak zâhir ve birçok müfessirînin muhtârı da budur.

ELMALILI:68:1-6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r12.claim: Besides the letter, Arabic nūn can mean fish, as in the reference to Jonah in al-Anbiya 21:87; it can also mean an inkpot and other things.
ELMALILI:68:1-6/r12.anchor: Arabîde نُون ismi bu harften başka olarak Hazret-i Yûnus’a وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r1.claim: Some identify Nūn with the great fish Yehmūt, on which the earths rest.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r1.anchor: Bazıları demiştir ki: Nûn büyük balıktır ki arzlar

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Ibn Abbas that God first created the Pen; its decree covered all future events, then vapor formed the heavens, Nūn was created, and the earth spread on it; its shaking led to mountains anchoring it.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r2.anchor: İbn Cerîr İbn Abbas’tan bu babda şunları rivayet eyler: Birincisi; Allah teâlâ’nın ilk halkettiği şey Kalem’dir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r3.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says the Pen was first, was commanded to write everything until Resurrection, and then Nūn was created on water and the earth spread over it.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r3.anchor: Bir diğeri: “Rabbimin ilk halkettiği şey Kalem’dir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r4.claim: Alusi transmits an Ibn Abbas hadith through Ziya and others; al-Hakim grades it authentic, and it says earth spread over Nūn, its convulsion shook earth, and mountains stabilized it before Ibn Abbas recited this verse.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r4.anchor: ve Hâkim’in sahih diye ve daha birtakımlarının İbn Abbas’tan rivayet eyledikleri bir hadis olmak üzere şöyle nakletmiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r5.claim: Mujahid’s report calls the supporting Nūn a fish, which made that description popular; the author says it is not an ordinary fish and warns against mistaken inferences.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r5.anchor: Fakat Mücâhid’den rivayette buna Arz’ın veya arzların üzerinde bulunduğu hût tâbir edilmiş

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r6.claim: He reconciles the reports as a creation sequence: the Pen of decree is a spiritual first principle, called by some the First Intellect or Muhammadan Light, followed by matter and cosmic bodies formed from vapor.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r6.anchor: İbtidâ Kalem-i A‘lâ denilen ve takdîr-i ezelîde kıyamete kadar cereyan edecek şeylerin bir projesini yapan

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r7.claim: Earth’s spherical liquid material separated from the heavens and was called Nūn or Hūt; later its crust formed as a shell spread over that sphere.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r7.anchor: ki “fezâ” dediğimiz semâ deryâsında yüzen bu maddeye kürevî olduğu anlatılmak üzere

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r8.claim: As the crust enclosed the liquid core, its constrained convulsions caused earthquakes, cracks, and volcanoes; accumulated earth waves formed mountains that stabilized the planet, as reflected by the Quranic term awtād, pegs.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r8.anchor: o Nûn evvelkisi gibi teneffüs edemeyerek nefesi tıkanmış bir balık gibi ıztırap ile deprenmeye başladığından bu sebeple hareket-i Arz, yani zelzeleler husûle gelmeye

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r9.claim: Mountain formation greatly benefited life; earthquakes, subsidence, volcanoes, and new or collapsing mountains still occur, but are minor compared with the earliest period and do not make the earth uninhabitable.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r9.anchor: Dağların teşekkülünün bu suretle Arz üzerinde hayat için büyük fâideleri olmuş ve bundan dolayı onların Arz’a karşı tefâhürle yukarıdan bakmaya bir hakları vardır.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r10.claim: The earth and mountains could suddenly disintegrate into scattered dust, as will be described in Sūrat al-Hāqqa; the author considers such an event possible at any time.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r10.anchor: bir lahzada un gibi dağılıp hebâen mensûrâ edilivermesi de her gün ihtimal dâhilindedir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r11.claim: Present earthquakes, subsidence, and volcanoes are movements of the Nūn by God’s command; fissures, eruptions, depressions, mountains, hills, and plains are lines written by the Supreme Pen.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r11.anchor: vukū‘bulmakta olan zelzeleler, hasifler, volkanlar dahi demek ki hep Arz’ın altındaki

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r12.claim: He argues that contemporary geological conclusions about the earth’s formation, mountains, and earthquakes amount to the same account given by these reports.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r12.anchor: zamanımızda Arz’ın teşekkülü ve dağların tekevvünü ve zelzelelerin tehaddüsü hakkında fen nâmına

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r13.claim: People on both sides mock the fish and geological accounts without understanding one another, sometimes branding each other ignorant or unbelieving; both err by forgetting that God commands the process.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r13.anchor: iki tarafta da bunun Allah’ın emriyle olmasını unutandır ki cehalet eder.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r14.claim: Some commentaries call the earth’s central sphere Hūt-i Aʿẓam or Yehmūt; some read Behmūt, but Qadi’s gloss specifies Yehmūt, with an alternative vowel pattern suggesting an intensive form.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r14.anchor: Bunu bâ ile mübhemiyetten “Behmût” okuyanlar olmuş ise de Kâdî hâşiyelerinde

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r15.claim: He derives Yehmūt from words for madness, raging attackers such as a flood or camel, and the boundless desert or severe famine; it can then denote volcano or space and the earth’s imprisoned, compressed, eruptive core.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r15.anchor: “Yehem” cünun; “eyhemân” iki saldırıcı ki bedeviler sel ile adama saldıran kızgın esrik deveye, medenîler de sel ile yangına derler.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r16.claim: The names describe different aspects: Yehmūt’s severity and terror, Hūt’s convulsion, and Nūn’s groan or circular rotation around the center.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r16.anchor: içine şiddet ve dehşeti itibariyle “Yehemût”, ıztırâbı itibariyle “Hût”, iniltisi veya merkez etrafında istidâresi itibariyle de “Nûn” denilmiş demek olur.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r17.speaker: مفسرون
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r17.claim: Some exegetes, relying on the reports, take Nūn as an oath by the fish, meaning Yehmūt.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r17.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirîn zikrolunan rivayetlere binâen burada “Nûn”, hût, yani balık mânasına

ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r18.speaker: مفسرون
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r18.claim: Other exegetes identify the Nūn with Jonah’s fish: al-Qalam calls Jonah the companion of the fish, al-Anbiya calls him Dhū al-Nūn, and al-Saffat says the fish swallowed him.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#2/r18.anchor: Bir kısmı da sûrede فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌۭ buyurulmuş olması

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r1.speaker: İbn Abbas, Dahhâk, Hasan, Katâde
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda are reported to prefer reading nūn as an inkpot.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r1.anchor: Yine İbn Abbas’tan mervî ve Dahhâk ve Hasan ve Katâde’nin muhtârı olarak bazıları da burada “nûn” devat

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r2.speaker: İbn Atıyye ve Râzî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Rāzī cite an anonymous poet’s use of nūn as evidence for the sense “inkpot.”
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r2.anchor: İbn Atıyye ve Râzî bir şâirin şu beytiyle de istişhad eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r3.claim: On the inkpot reading, the oath is by inkpot and pen because writing is done with them; books and writing are highly important and useful, though the pen alone conveys this too.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r3.anchor: Çünkü yazı bunlarla yazılır. Nutuk gibi kitab

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r4.speaker: Muâviye b. Kurre
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r4.claim: Muʿāwiya b. Qurra is said to transmit as a Prophetic report that nūn is a tablet of light.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r4.anchor: Muâviye b. Kurre’nin bunu bir hadîs-i merfû‘olarak naklettiği zikrolunmuştur

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r5.claim: Elmalılı suggests the light-tablet image may derive from the sun or earth appearing as a n-shaped point in the sky’s arc.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r5.anchor: Bu mâna; ufukta semâ kavsi içinde bir nokta gibi bulunan Güneş’in veya Arz’ın bir ن şekli resmetmesinden müste‘âr olabilir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r6.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to identify nūn as the final letter of the name al-Raḥmān.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r6.anchor: Yine İbn Abbas’tan: اَل َّرحْمٰنُ harflerinin son harfidir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r7.speaker: Ca‘fer-i Sâdık
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r7.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is reported to say that nūn is a river in Paradise.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r7.anchor: Ca‘fer-i Sâdık Hazretleri’nden: Cennet nehirlerinden bir nehirdir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r8.claim: The lexicon also gives nūn as inkpot, fish, sword-edge, a fish-shaped sword, a correct word, and the dimple in an infant’s chin (nūna).
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r8.anchor: Kāmûs’ta mezkur olduğu üzere “nûn” devat ve hût mânasına geldiği gibi şefretü’s-seyf, yani kılıcın ağzına da denir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r9.claim: Since the feminine suffix marks singularity, nūn can be a generic noun for sword and the oath could be by sword and pen, although no report supports this reading here.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r9.anchor: Şu hâlde “nûn” ism-i cins olarak نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ kılıç ve kaleme kasem olmak da muhtemildir. Lâkin burada buna dair bir rivayet vârid olmamıştır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r10.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r10.claim: The Kashshāf author takes nūn as an alphabetic letter: if it were a noun, its case and tanwīn or proper-name inflection would be missing, and its syntactic role unexplained; fish, tablet, and river readings face the same problem.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r10.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf demiştir ki: “Murad, hurûf-i mu‘cemden olan bu ن harfidir. Divit demelerine gelince, vaz‘-ı lügavî midir, yoksa şer‘î midir bilmem.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r11.speaker: İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid are cited for identifying nūn as the name of the great whale.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r11.anchor: Onun hût-i a‘zamın ismi olduğuna dair İbn Abbas ve Mücâhid’den

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r12.speaker: Ebû Hayyan
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r12.claim: Abū Ḥayyān regards nūn as an ungoverned disjoint letter like ṣād and qāf, and says the transmitted identifications as whale, inkpot, tablet, al-Raḥmān’s last letter, or heavenly river are likely unsound.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r12.anchor: Ebû Hayyan da demiştir ki: “ن hurûf-i mu‘cemeden ص, ق gibi bir harftir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r13.speaker: Ebû Nasr Abdurrahîm Kuşeyrî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī likewise says nūn is an alphabetic initial: if it were a complete word it would inflect like qalam, as do other sūra openings.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r13.anchor: Ebû Nasr Abdurrahîm Kuşeyrî de tefsirinde; ن hurûf-i mu‘cemeden bir harftir. Tam bir kelime olsaydı ‘kalem’ gibi i‘rab olunurdu

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r14.claim: Elmalılı concludes that nūn is simply an alphabetic letter in writing and pronunciation, named as in reciting alif-bā; its basic function is challenge and testing the deeply rooted.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r14.anchor: Bizim bütün bunlardan vâsıl olduğumuz netice de şudur: Evet, resm-i hat ve lafız nokta-i nazarından burada ن sade bir hecâ harfidir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r15.claim: Being a letter does not prevent nūn from naming the sūra or serving as an ambiguous symbol that rationally suggests multiple meanings.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r15.anchor: Lâkin böyle olması sûrenin ismi olmasına mâni‘olmayacağı gibi, birçok mânalara delâlet-i akliye ile muhtemil müteşabih bir remz olmasını da mâni‘değil, muktezîdir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r16.claim: One should not insist that a single possible sense is the intended one; reports about familiar meanings should not be rejected when they are not very weak and have intelligible, useful interpretations.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r16.anchor: Bundan dolayı “nûn” lafzının zihinleri sürükleyebileceği muhtemil mânalardan birini “murad budur” diyerek hasra kalkışmak doğru olmaz

ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r17.claim: Elmalılı reads Ibn ʿAbbās’s multiple reports as separate possible aspects, each offered with a benefit, rather than as mutually exclusive claims to the sole intended meaning.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#3/r17.anchor: Zira İbn Abbas’tan rivayetlerin ta‘addüdü gösteriyor ki o onları tahsis için birer vech olmak üzere söylemiş ve her birinde bir fâide beyan eylemiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r1.claim: Elmalılı says to recall reports about the first-created pen when considering nūn, yet its intended sense remains among the ambiguous matters whose interpretation only God knows (3:7).
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r1.anchor: أَ َّولُ مَا خَلَقَ االلهُ الْقَلَمَ fıkrası ve şu hâlde nûn sesinden hatıra gelebilen

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r2.claim: Although the recitation makes nūn’s literal identity as a disjoint letter certain, this does not remove ambiguity: its relation to pen and writing must be inferred, making it a symbol with further possible senses.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r2.anchor: Lâkin burada bu kadarı teşabühün ref‘i için

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r3.claim: It cannot be determined whether nūn itself contains an oath; if it does, the wāw before al-qalam is oath wāw, while the wāw before mā is connective.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r3.anchor: Şu hâlde ن bir kasemi tazammun ediyor mu etmiyor mu kestirilemez. Kasem mukadder ise {وَٱلْقَلَمِ}deki vâv, وَمَا’deki gibi atıf için değil ise kasem için olur

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r4.claim: Commentators give two analyses of al-qalam: the definite article may mark a particular known pen (ʿahd) or the genus of pens.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r4.anchor: Müfessirîn burada iki vecih söylemişlerdir. Birisi “lâm”ın ahd

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r5.speaker: İbn Cerîr
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r5.claim: Ibn Jarīr identifies the known pen as the one God created and commanded to write what would occur through the Resurrection.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r5.anchor: İbn Cerîr der ki: “‘Kalem’, mâruf olan kalemdir. Şu kadar ki Rabbimizin kalemler içinde kasem ettiği kalem o kalemdir ki Teâlâ zikruhu halkedip emretmiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r6.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r6.claim: The Prophet reports that God first created the Pen and ordered it to write the decree, which it recorded for all that had happened and would happen forever; ʿUbāda’s deathbed counsel to his son stresses faith in good and bad destiny.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r6.anchor: Ben Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Hazretleri’ni dinledim, diyordu ki: إ َّن أ َّولَ مَا خَلَقَ االلهُ خَلَقَ القَلَمَ فَقالَ لَهُ: اكْتُبْ

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r7.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses “nūn and the Pen” as that by which remembrance is written.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r7.anchor: Mücâhid’den de نٓ وَٱلْقَلَمِ kendisiyle zikir yazılandır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r8.claim: Elmalılı concludes that the referential Pen is the one that writes the Preserved Tablet or the Qurʾān.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r8.anchor: Demek ki kasem olunan kalem şer‘an ma‘hud olan kalemdir ki o da Levh-i Mahfûz’u yazan kalem yahut Kur’an yazılan kalemdir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r9.claim: Other commentators take al-qalam generically, as in “taught by the pen” (96:4).
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r9.anchor: olduğu gibi cinse hamledenler de vardır.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r10.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r10.claim: The Kashshāf says the oath honors the Pen because its creation and design display immense wisdom and its benefits exceed description.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r10.anchor: Keşşâf şöyle der: “Kaleme kasem buyurdu, şânına tâzim için, çünkü onun halk ve tesviyesinde hikmet-i azîmeye delâlet vardır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r11.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says those who identify nūn as Behmūt take the Pen to be the cosmic pen God created and commanded to write the universe, with yasturun’s pronoun referring to angels.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r12.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explicitly identifies the subject of yasturun as people when the Pen means the familiar human writing tool.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r12.anchor: İbn Abbas bunu tansis eylemiş ve يَسْطُرُونَ’daki zamiri de ‘nâs’a göndermiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r13.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats the oath as covering writing as a whole, the foundation of knowledge and worldly and afterlife affairs; the Pen is the tongue’s sibling and a universal divine gift.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r14.speaker: İmâm Râzî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī’s generic reading includes pens used in heaven and earth: God’s gifts of speech and writing (55:3–4; 96:3–5) let people communicate beyond those nearby.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r14.anchor: İmâm Râzî de şöyle der: “‘Ve’l-kalem’de iki kavil vardır, birisi budur ki kasem edilen kalem, gerek semâda bulunanın ve gerek Arz’da bulunanın yazdığı kalemin hepsine vâki‘olan cinstir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r15.speaker: İmâm Râzî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r15.claim: Al-Rāzī’s second view is the particular first-created Pen, a luminous pen stretching between heaven and earth that writes events, lifespans, and deeds until the Hour.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r15.anchor: ma‘hud kalemdir. Allah teâlâ bunu evvelâ halketmiş, sonra da ona kıyamete kadar olacağı

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r16.speaker: Kādî (Ebû Bekr Bâkıllânî olmalı)
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r16.claim: The Qāḍī, probably Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī, reads the command to the Pen metaphorically: a writing tool is not a living, accountable intellect, so “write” means God brings events about by effective power, as in 2:117.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r16.anchor: Kādî (Ebû Bekr Bâkıllânî olmalı) demiştir ki: ‘Bu haberi mecâza hamletmek îcab eder. Çünkü kitabette âlet-i mahsûsa olan kalem emr ü nehy olunacak hay ve âkıl değildir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r17.speaker: İmâm Râzî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r17.claim: Al-Rāzī reports the claim that the Pen is intellect, the source of creatures: reports naming the first creation as Pen, intellect, or a primordial substance are reconciled as describing one thing.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r17.anchor: Yine Râzî der ki: “Nâstan bazı kimseler de şu zu‘mda bulunmuştur: Burada mezkur olan kalem akıldır.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r18.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r18.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī summarizes al-qalam as either the writer of the Tablet or the instrument used for writing; it is sworn by because its benefits are numerous.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r18.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî de bunları şöyle hulâsa eder: “Ve’l-kalem, Levh’i yazan, yahut kendisiyle yazılandır. Ona kasem buyuruldu. Çünkü fevâidi çoktur

ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r19.speaker: Suyûtî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r19.claim: Al-Jalālayn says the Pen is that by which the universe was written on the Preserved Tablet; Elmalılı says al-qalam could sound generic, but al-Suyūṭī intends a particular known Pen.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#4/r19.anchor: Tefsîr-i Celâleyn’de de der ki: “Kalem kâinâtın Levh-i Mahfuz’da yazıldığıdır.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r1.claim: The particular Pen also belongs to the genus; the familiar human pen taught in 96:4 is the plain example, and human writing has recorded thought and memory from creation onward and will continue.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r1.anchor: Mâlum ki ma‘hud da cins cümlesindendir. عَلَّمَ بِالْقَلَمِ mısdâkınca insana tâlim olunan cins-i kalemden zâhir olan ise mâlumumuz olan kalem-i beşer görünür

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r2.claim: Even when the oath refers to one particular Pen, it honors the genus of pens and therefore also gives dignity to the human pen.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r2.anchor: gerek hakikat gerek mecaz her ne mâna ile olursa olsun kaleme kasem edilince bundan bir ferd-i ma‘hud

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r3.claim: With a general audience, the human pen would be the apparent sense, as in 96:4–5; under a particular reference, one or several pens may be intended, and metaphor may point to the primordial pen of nature.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r3.anchor: Eğer bu kasemin cevâbında muhatab bilhassa Hazret-i Peygamber’in kendisi olmasaydı da hitâb-ı âm olsa idi, burada عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ [el-Alâk 96/4-5] gibi kalem-i beşer murad olunmak zâhir olurdu

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.claim: Because the address is specifically to Muḥammad, recipient of divine favor and noble character, who neither read nor wrote before revelation nor knew the Book (29:48; 42:52), Elmalılı prefers the divine primordial Pen, also called the First or Highest Pen; he finds this view in Ibn Jarīr and al-Jalālayn.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.anchor: Fakat burada hitab bilhassa ni‘met-i ilâhiyeye mazhar kılınarak, وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ [el-Kalem 68/4] buyurulan zât-ı Hazret-i Muhammedî’ye ait olması

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r5.claim: In uṣūl terms, al-qalam explicitly denotes the divine Pen and indicates the human pen by implication; those saying “genus” encompass both literal and metaphorical senses but do not distinguish explicit text from apparent indication.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r5.anchor: Bu وَٱلْقَلَمِ’de “kalem”, kalem-i ilâhîde bi’l-ibâre nas, dolayısıyla kalem-i beşer hakkında da bi’l-işâre zâhir demektir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r6.claim: The definite article is not exhaustive: the oath does not honor every pen, and Elmalılı says no commentator takes it as alif-lām of total inclusion.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r6.anchor: Sonra şunu da unutmamak lâzım gelir ki bu وَٱلْقَلَمِ’de elif lâmın istiğrak için olduğuna kāil olan yoktur

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r7.claim: Pens used to falsify truth, harm God’s servants, and spread discord through malice, immorality, or stupidity are pens but deserve no praise for truth and goodness.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r7.anchor: Zira hakkı ibtal veya ibâdullahı ızrar yolunda şeytanet ve ahlâksızlık veya idraksizlikle

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.claim: The following denial of madness, affirmation of divine favor, understanding, character, and great reward, and condemnation of immoral liars clarify which side of the pen’s significance is praised.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.anchor: Bundan dolayı burada bu kasemin arkasından cünûnun, fitnenin nefyi ve ni‘met-i rabbâniyenin idrak ve ahlâkın, ecrin büyüklüğünü beyan ve ahlâksızların, yalancıların zemmi ile o cihete de tenbih buyurulacaktır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r9.claim: Elmalılı’s rendering addresses Muḥammad: pause over the opening called Nūn; he swears by it, the known Pen of Truth, and what the people of the Pen have written and will write.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r9.anchor: ve ehl-i kalemin satıra dizip yazdıklarına ve yazacaklarına ki yâ Muhammed!

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r10.claim: Yasturun is a sound masculine plural, normally used for rational beings; attributing writing to an unmentioned rational plural behind the singular Pen points to its unseen intelligent users as the real writers.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r10.anchor: “Kalem” müfred olarak zikrolunduğu hâlde yazış ve yazılanlar ona nisbet edilmeyip

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r11.claim: The visible tool signifies its hidden rational user; the Pen stands for the writing it produces, and the connective wāw joins an oath encompassing the Pen, writings, and their intelligent authors.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r11.anchor: “Kalem”den maksud da kendisi değil, o yazdıklarıdır, وَمَا,وَٱلْقَلَمِ’daki vâv-ı atıf gibi bir âlettir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r12.claim: From pen and writing one should infer the world of intellects and meanings, then the First Pen that writes them into human intellect, and finally its Lord, the Lord of the worlds.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r12.anchor: Bu suretle burada vâv atıf için olarak kasem, kalem ve yazılarıyla sâhipleri olan ehl-i idrâke delâlet etmek üzere mecmû‘una yapılmıştır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r13.claim: For the human Pen, its writers are rational people—consciousness and intelligence rather than visible bodies; for the Highest Pen, angels write forms of things and meanings, while God writes them.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r13.anchor: Kalem-i beşere nazaran yazıcılar ehl-i kalem, akıl ve idrak sâhibi insanlar, hem de göze görünen bedenler değil, insanlık hakikatini teşkil eden şuurlar, zekâlar olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r14.claim: The pronoun in yasturun can refer to human writers with the human Pen or to angels with the Highest Pen, explaining why commentaries give either “people” or “angels.”
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r14.anchor: Bunun için burada وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ’un fâili olan zamir kalem-i beşere nazaran müdrik insanlara işaret olduğu gibi, Kalem-i A‘lâ’ya nazaran da melâike olmak üzere tefsir edilmiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r15.claim: Turkish lacks the sound masculine plural form, so “the Pen and what they write” does not express the shift from the instrument to its intelligent users.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r15.anchor: Lisânımızda böyle cem‘-i müzekker-i sâlim sîgası bulunmadığı için bu nükte

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r16.claim: Yasturun is imperfective and indicates continuity into the present and future; Turkish translations cannot capture all of this tense and aspect nuance.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r16.anchor: Bir de يَسْطُرُونَ muzâri‘sîgasıdır. İstimrâra ve hâl ü istikbâle delâlet eder

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r17.claim: The Highest Pen was active when these verses descended and continues to write; the report that the Pen has dried means what has occurred is written, not that writing of future events has ceased.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r17.anchor: Bu bize şunu da anlatmış oluyorki bu âyetler nâzil olurken Kalem-i A‘lâ cereyan ediyordu ve daha edecektir.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r18.claim: Complete finality in decree pertains to God’s knowledge, the Mother of the Book; with respect to the Preserved Tablet and created existence, God erases and establishes (13:39).
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r18.anchor: Kaderde ferâğ-ı tâm Ümmü’l-Kitâb olan ilmullâha nazarandır. Yoksa Levh-i Mahfûz’a ve sâha-i tekvîne nazaran يَمْحُوا۟ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثْبِتُ’dir [er-Ra‘d 13/39]

ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r5.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r5.claim: Some interpreters identify the opening nun as the fish in which Jonah was confined.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r5.anchor: Bundan bazıları نٓ’dan murad bu hût olduğuna zâhib olmuşlardır.

ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r6.claim: Elmalılı rejects the fish as the primary meaning of nun because, on that reading, the verse would more fittingly say Sahib al-Nun, though an allusion remains.
ELMALILI:68:40-50#4/r6.anchor: Lâkin öyle olsa idi burada “sâhibi’n-nûn” denilmek muvâfık olurdu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r1.claim: The opening nūn is a disjointed letter and the first of this class to be revealed; the commentary refers readers to 2:1 for fuller discussion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r1.anchor: Sûrenin başında bulunan “nûn” harfi, “hurûf-ı mukattaa”dan olup bu tür harflerin ilk inenidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.claim: In response, God swears by the pen and writers' lines to deny that the Prophet is mad and affirm his divine favor, namely the honor of prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.anchor: Allah Teâlâ kaleme ve kalem ehlinin yazdığı satırlara yemin ederek onun, iddia edildiği gibi mecnun olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r4.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r4.claim: Elmalılı says the verb form makes intelligent beings, rather than pens, the actual writers, and the passage indicates that “pen” means what it writes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r4.anchor: Elmalılı buradaki bir anlam inceliğine dikkat çekerken özetle şunları söyler: “(Yazanların) yazdıklarına” diye çevrilen cümledeki fiilin kalıbı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r5.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r5.claim: Elmalılı traces pen and writing to the realm of reason and meanings, then to the first pen that inscribes them in human intellect and its owner, the Lord of the worlds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r5.anchor: kalem ve yazılardan, akıl ve anlamlar âlemini, bunlardan da onları beşer aklına yazan ilk kalemi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r6.speaker: Elmalılı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r6.claim: Elmalılı notes that the verb encompasses both what writers are writing and what they will write.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r6.anchor: bu fiilin, “yazmakta oldukları ve yazacakları” anlamlarını birlikte anlattığı da gözden kaçırılmamalıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r7.speaker: unnamed commentators
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r7.claim: Some identify the pen as the pen that writes revelation and its written contents as the Qur'an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r7.anchor: “Kalemden maksat vahyi yazan kalem, yazdıklarından maksat Kur’an’dır” diyenler de olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r8.claim: The author prefers the general interpretation: writing transmits thought, experience, and understanding across people, generations, and cultures, preserves knowledge, and advances learning and civilization.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r8.anchor: âyeti genel anlamda değerlendirmek daha doğru olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r9.claim: The oath honors written culture: the first revealed surah begins with “Read,” while this second revealed surah opens by swearing by the pen and its writers' work.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r9.anchor: ilk inen sûresine (Alak) “oku!” buyruğuyla başlandığı gibi ikinci inen bu sûrenin ilk âyetinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r10.claim: The verses helped encourage the Hijaz Arabs' transition to written culture alongside other causes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r10.anchor: Hicaz Bölgesi Araplarının ilk defa Kur’an ile birlikte yazılı kültüre geçmelerinde –başka âmiller yanında– bu gibi âyetlerin teşvik edici bir role sahip olduğu

BURHAN:v1p377/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.claim: The author holds that writing was divinely taught, citing God’s teaching by the pen and the Quranic oath by the pen; Adam and other prophets may have been taught it.
BURHAN:v1p377/r2.anchor: والذى نقوله إن الخط توقيفي لقوله ﴿ علم بالقلم علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم ﴾ وقال تعالى ﴿ ن والقلم وما يسطرون ﴾

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r1.claim: Whoever witnesses God's gentleness does not abase himself before creatures or seek help from dependent beings; he thanks God for gifts and praises Him beautifully in deprivation.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r1.anchor: من شهد لطفه لم يتلل بعدع لمخلوق

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies Nūn as the whale bearing the cosmos on its back.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r2.anchor: قيل : الحوت الذي على ظهره الكون

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes Nūn to mean an inkwell.

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r4.claim: Another takes the letter as the key to divine names Nāṣir and Nūr.

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r5.claim: Another explanation says the oath invokes God's support for His believing servants.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r5.anchor: أقسم بنصرة الله تعالى لعباده المؤمنين

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r6.claim: The oath by the pen is answered by the assurance that Muhammad is not mad and has an undiminished reward.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r6.anchor: وأقسم بالقلم - وجواب القسم قوله : { مآ أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون وإن لك لأجرا غير ممنون }

BURHAN:v1p170#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r1.claim: Basrans count none of the disconnected openings as verses; Kufans count some by transmitted convention, with different counts for each letter opening. Al-Wāḥidī instead counts only Ṭā Hā, whose ending matches what follows.
BURHAN:v1p170#2/r1.anchor: وهو علم توقيفى لا مجال للقياس فيه كمعرفة السور

BURHAN:v1p148/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p148/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p148/r1.claim: The writing of ولما uses wāw in Hud and Yusuf; elsewhere it is written بالفاء.
BURHAN:v1p148/r1.anchor: بالواو فى هود ويوسف وفى غيرهما بالفاء

BURHAN:v1p148/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p148/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p148/r2.claim: The Qur'anic script separates أن لا in ten places, including al-Qalam.
BURHAN:v1p148/r2.anchor: ﴿ أن لا ﴾ تكتب فى المصحف بالنون منفصلة عشرة

BURHAN:v1p170/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p170/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p170/r1.claim: Surat al-Qalam's endings share one rhythm, and its vocabulary repeatedly features the letter nun.
BURHAN:v1p170/r1.anchor: فإن فواصلها كلها على هذا الوزن مع ما تضمنت من الألفاظ النونية

BURHAN:v1p170/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p170/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p170/r7.claim: The usual pattern is to follow the disjoint letters with material about the Qur'an, as in المص ذلك الكتاب; the author asks why al-Ankabut and al-Rum differ.
BURHAN:v1p170/r7.anchor: واعلم أن عادة القرآن العظيم فى ذكر هذه الحروف أن يذكر بعدها ما يتعلق بالقرآن

ITQAN:v3p22/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p22/r8.speaker: سالم بن عبد الله
ITQAN:v3p22/r8.claim: Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah says alif-lam-mim, ḥā-mīm, nūn, and similar openings are divine names split into letters.
ITQAN:v3p22/r8.anchor: وأخرج عن سالم بن عبد الله قال ﴿ الم ﴾ و ﴿ حم ﴾ و ﴿ ن ﴾ ونحوها اسم الله مقطعة

ITQAN:v3p22/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p22/r11.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v3p22/r11.claim: Another scholar says nun is a key to the divine names Nur and Nasir.
ITQAN:v3p22/r11.anchor: وحكى غيره في قوله ﴿ ن ﴾ إنه مفتاح اسمه تعالى نور وناصر

ITQAN:v4p532#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet saying the first created things were the Pen and Whale; the Pen was told to write everything destined through Judgment Day, and ن is the Whale.
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r1.anchor: أخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إن أول ما خلق الله القلم والحوت

ITQAN:v4p532#4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r2.claim: Muawiya ibn Qurra's father reports the Prophet identifying ن and the Pen as a tablet and pen of light that record what will happen until the Resurrection; Ibn Kathir calls the report mursal and gharib.
ITQAN:v4p532#4/r2.anchor: عن معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ن والقلم وما يسطرون لوح من نور وقلم من نور

SULAMI:v2p343/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p343/r1.claim: Nun is a name of God: combining the opening letters alif-lam-ra, ha-mim, and nun yields al-Rahman.
SULAMI:v2p343/r1.anchor: قال سهل : النون اسم من أسماء الله وذلك انه إذا جمعت أوائل هذه الثلاث سور ﴿ الر ﴾ و ﴿ حم ﴾ و ﴿ ن ﴾ يكون الرحمن

SULAMI:v2p343/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SULAMI:v2p343/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says nun is the inkwell with which the Reminder was written, and what was written on the Preserved Tablet about felicity and misery.
SULAMI:v2p343/r2.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس انه قال : النون الدواة التي كتب بها الذكر وما يسطرون

SULAMI:v2p343/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v2p343/r3.claim: What is written is the script that God taught His servants.
SULAMI:v2p343/r3.anchor: وقيل : وما يسطرون من الخط الذي تولى الله تعليمه لعباده

SULAMI:v2p343/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p343/r4.claim: Nun is pre-eternity from which all lights were originated and specially bestowed upon Muhammad; his great character is the pre-eternal light singled out for him.
SULAMI:v2p343/r4.anchor: قال جعفر : نون الأزلية الذي اخترع منه الأنوار كلها فجعل ذلك لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فلذلك قيل له

SULAMI:v2p343/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p343/r5.claim: Another interpretation identifies nun as the power, the pen as the decree, and those writing as the noble recording angels.
SULAMI:v2p343/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : النون نون القدرة وقلم القضاء وما يسطرون الملائكة الكرام الكاتبون

ITQAN:v1p255/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p255/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p255/r14.claim: The sixteenth case is the nūn assimilated into wāw in ن والقلم.
ITQAN:v1p255/r14.anchor: السادس عشر النون فيها من ﴿ ن والقلم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p29/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p29/r1.claim: One reported interpretation takes ن as an oath by Muhammad’s strength of heart.
ITQAN:v3p29/r1.anchor: وقيل أقسم بقوة قلب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v3p29/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p29/r2.claim: Another reported view identifies the letter with the kāf in قضي الأمر, indicating the rest of the word.
ITQAN:v3p29/r2.anchor: وقيل هي الكاف من قوله ﴿ قضي الأمر ﴾ دلت على بقية الكلمة

ITQAN:v3p29/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r3.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v3p29/r3.claim: Al-Kirmani reports that ن means “persist, Muhammad,” in delivering the message and doing what you were commanded.
ITQAN:v3p29/r3.anchor: وقيل معناها قف يا محمد على أداء الرسالة والعمل بما أمرت حكاهما الكرماني

ITQAN:v3p29/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p29/r4.claim: A marfu‘ report from Ibn Abbas says the first created things were the Pen and the whale; God commanded the Pen to record everything through Judgment Day, identifying ن as the whale.
ITQAN:v3p29/r4.anchor: أخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس مرفوعا

ITQAN:v3p29/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r5.speaker: ابن قرة
ITQAN:v3p29/r5.claim: A marfu‘ report transmitted by Ibn Jarir through the mursal Ibn Qurrah identifies ن as the Preserved Tablet.
ITQAN:v3p29/r5.anchor: وقيل هو اللوح المحفوظ أخرجه ابن جرير من مرسل ابن قرة مرفوعا

ITQAN:v3p29/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ITQAN:v3p29/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada are reported to interpret ن as an inkwell.
ITQAN:v3p29/r6.anchor: وقيل هو الدواة أخرجه عن الحسن وقتادة

ITQAN:v3p29/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r7.speaker: ابن قرصة
ITQAN:v3p29/r7.claim: Ibn Qursa says ن means ink.
ITQAN:v3p29/r7.anchor: وقيل هو المداد حكاه ابن قرصة في غريبه

ITQAN:v3p29/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r8.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v3p29/r8.claim: Al-Kirmani, transmitting al-Jahiz’s view, says ن means the Pen.
ITQAN:v3p29/r8.anchor: وقيل هو القلم حكاه الكرماني عن الجاحظ

ITQAN:v3p29/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r9.speaker: ابن عساكر
ITQAN:v3p29/r9.claim: Ibn Asakir records the view that ن is one of the Prophet’s names.
ITQAN:v3p29/r9.anchor: وقيل هو اسم من أسماء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حكاه ابن عساكر

ITQAN:v3p29/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p29/r11.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v3p29/r11.claim: Ibn Jinni argues that this reading shows the opening letters separate suras; if they were divine names, they could not be altered because proper names must be preserved exactly.
ITQAN:v3p29/r11.anchor: قال ابن جني وفي هذه القراءة دليل على أن الفواتح فواصل بين السور ولو كانت أسماء الله لم يجز تحريف شيء منها

ITQAN:v4p442/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r1.speaker: ابن العباس المراكشي
ITQAN:v4p442/r1.claim: Al-Marrakushi wrote a work explaining orthographic departures from standard script and argued that letter forms vary with the meanings of the words.
ITQAN:v4p442/r1.anchor: منه أبو العباس المراكشي كتابا سماه ( عنوان الدليل في مرسوم خط التنزيل )

ITQAN:v4p442/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r2.speaker: كعب الأحبار
ITQAN:v4p442/r2.claim: Ka‘b al-Ahbar’s report says Adam established Arabic, Syriac, and all scripts in clay before his death; after the Flood, each people received its script, and Ishmael received Arabic.
ITQAN:v4p442/r2.anchor: عن كعب الأحبار قال أول من وضع الكتاب العربي والسرياني والكتب كلها آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p442/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p442/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ishmael first established Arabic writing as one continuous sequence; his sons Humsay‘ and Qaydar later separated the words.
ITQAN:v4p442/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أول من وضع الكتاب العربي إسماعيل وضع الكتاب كله على لفظه ومنطقه

ITQAN:v4p442/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p442/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the first writing sent down by God from heaven was أبجد.
ITQAN:v4p442/r4.anchor: من طريق سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال أول كتاب أنزله الله من السماء أبو جاد

ITQAN:v4p442/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.claim: Ibn Faris argues that script was taught by God, citing the verses about the Pen and teaching humanity; these letters belong among the names taught to Adam.
ITQAN:v4p442/r5.anchor: وقال ابن فارس الذي نقوله إن الخط توقيفي لقوله تعالى

TUSTARI:68:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:1/r1.claim: Nun is a name of God; joined to the initial letters alif-lam-ra and ha-mim, it forms the name الرحمن.
TUSTARI:68:1/r1.anchor: النون اسم من أسماء الله تعالى، إذا جمعت بين أوائل السور:

TUSTARI:68:1/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TUSTARI:68:1/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets nun as the inkwell from which the remembrance was written, and the pen as that which wrote the wise remembrance.
TUSTARI:68:1/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: النون الدواة التي كتب الذكر منها، والقلم الذي كتب به الذكر الحكيم

TUSTARI:68:1/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:1/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:1/r3.claim: “What they write” is what the recording angels write of the deeds of Adam's children.
TUSTARI:68:1/r3.anchor: ما تكتبه الحفظة من أعمال بني آدم

TUSTARI:68:1/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:1/r4.speaker: عمر بن واصل
TUSTARI:68:1/r4.claim: Umar ibn Wasil says this is the writing God undertakes for His servants, containing benefits and welfare for people and lands.
TUSTARI:68:1/r4.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل: وما يسطرون، أي: وما تولى الله لعباده

DAMGHANI:v1p389/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r7.claim: Qalam can also mean the writing instrument itself, by which writing is made.
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r7.anchor: القلم بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة ن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r1.claim: Qalam can mean the writing instrument.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r1.anchor: القلم : يقال ويراد به الذي يكتب به . ويقال ويراد به القدح

FARRA:v3p172/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p172/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p172/r1.claim: Readers either pronounce or assimilate the final n of ن; al-Farrāʾ prefers pronunciation because letter names are spelled and treated as paused even when connected.
FARRA:v3p172/r1.anchor: تخفى النون الآخرة ، وتظهرها، وإظهارها أعجب إلي

FARRA:v3p172/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p172/r2.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
FARRA:v3p172/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Hamza pronounce the final n; other readers leave it unpronounced.
FARRA:v3p172/r2.anchor: كان الأعمش وحمزة يبينانها، وبعضهم يترك التبيان

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r1.speaker: قتادة والحسن
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r1.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan identify Nūn as an inkpot.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r1.anchor:
قال قتادة والحسن: (2) هي الدواة.
ويقال: الحوت تحت الأرض (3) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r2.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies Nūn as the fish beneath the earth.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r2.anchor:
قال قتادة والحسن: (2) هي الدواة.
ويقال: الحوت تحت الأرض (3) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r3.claim: He explains what they do as writing; he notes that he treated the disconnected letters elsewhere.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p477#2/r3.anchor: وقد ذكرت الحروف المقطعة في كتاب "تأويل مشكل القرآن" (4) . {وما يسطرون} أي يكتبون.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r1.claim: Astāṭīr means the written accounts of earlier people; satar means writing, and what they write is their writing. Ibn Qutayba rejects Abū ʿUbayda’s claim that the singular is usṭūra or isṭāra, meaning nonsense without order.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r1.anchor: {أساطير الأولين} أخبارهم. وما سطر منها أي كتب. ومنه قوله: {وما يسطرون} (2) أي يكتبون.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the singular of asāṭīr is usṭūra or isṭāra, meaning baseless tales without order; Ibn Qutayba rejects this analysis as unsound.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p37#2/r2.anchor: وأبو عبيدة (3) يجعل واحدها أسطورة وإسطارة [معناها الترهات البسابس] (4) وهو الذي لا نظام له. وليس بشيء صحيح.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r1.claim: God’s oath by the alphabet honors its letters as the building blocks of revealed books, divine names and attributes, and human speech and worship.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r1.anchor: وإنما أقسم الله بحروف المعجم، لشرفها وفضلها، ولأنها مباني كتبه المنزلة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r2.claim: The oath by the pen magnifies what people write; the fig and olive are named for two holy-land mountains that grow them, called in Syriac Ṭūr Zaytā and Ṭūr Tīnā.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r4.claim: If the opening letters abbreviate divine attributes, this follows Arab shorthand: words replace related words, and letters replace others with nearby articulation, as in مدهته for مدحته and جدث/جدف.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p183/r4.anchor: وإن كان حروفا مأخوذة من صفات الله، فهذا فن من اختصار العرب

MAJAZ:v2p264/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p264/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p264/r1.claim: Nūn and the Pen are treated like the other opening letters of the sūras.

MAJAZ:v2p264/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p264/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p264/r2.claim: Yasṭurūn means they write; Ruʾba’s line with asṭār is cited for the usage.

NAHHAS:v5p3/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
NAHHAS:v5p3/r1.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra gives a cosmology: earths rest on Nun, Nun on water, and water on a rock supported by four angels.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r1.anchor: روى الحكم بن ظهير عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة

NAHHAS:v5p3/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say المر وحم ون are disconnected letters of al-Raḥmān.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r2.anchor: وروى يزيد عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال المر وحم ون حروف الرحمن مقطعة

NAHHAS:v5p3/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r3.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
NAHHAS:v5p3/r3.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says Nun is a tablet of light.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r3.anchor: وفي حديث معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه مرفوعا قال ن لوح من نور

NAHHAS:v5p3/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r4.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p3/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses Nun as an inkwell.

NAHHAS:v5p3/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r5.claim: Other suggestions are ‘by the Lord of Nun’ with an omitted oath noun, or an attention particle like Alif Lām Mīm.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r5.anchor: وقيل التقدير ورب نون وقيل هو تنبيه كما تقدم في ألم

NAHHAS:v5p3/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r6.claim: Six pronunciations are recorded: clear, hidden, or assimilated nūn with or without nasalization, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar's reading, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq's genitive.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r6.anchor: قرأ أكثر الناس ( نون والقلم ) ببيان نون وقرىء بإخفائها وقرىء بإدغامها بغنة وبغير غنة

NAHHAS:v5p3/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r7.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
NAHHAS:v5p3/r7.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar is reported to read نون والقلم.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r7.anchor: وروي عن عيسى بن عمر أنه قرأ ( نون والقلم )

NAHHAS:v5p3/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r8.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v5p3/r8.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads Nun with kasra before the oath noun.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( نون والقلم ) بالخفض

NAHHAS:v5p3/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r9.speaker: الأخفش سعيد
NAHHAS:v5p3/r9.claim: For accusative Nun, al-Akhfash offers an understood أذكر or says it is indeclinable as a sūra or foreign name.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r9.anchor: منها أن تكون منصوبة بوقوع الفعل عليها أي أذكر نون ولم تنصرف لأنها اسم للسورة

NAHHAS:v5p3/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r10.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v5p3/r10.claim: Sibawayh says letter names are indeclinable because they resemble أين and كيف.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r10.anchor: وقول سيبويه إنها شبهت بأين وكيف

NAHHAS:v5p3/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p3/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ compares the form to ثم or to plural نون.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r11.anchor: وقول الفراء إنها شبهت بثم وقيل شبهت بنون الجميع

NAHHAS:v5p3/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v5p3/r12.claim: Abū Ḥātim says the oath wāw was omitted, leaving Nun accusative under an understood verb.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r12.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم حذفت منها واو القسم فانتصبت بإضمار فعل

NAHHAS:v5p3/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r13.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v5p3/r13.claim: Sibawayh says alphabet letters are uninflected because they are parts of words, like a word's middle letters.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r13.anchor: فمذهب سيبويه أن حروف المعجم إنما سكنت لأنها بعض حروف الأسماء

NAHHAS:v5p3/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r14.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p3/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ's teaching-the-alphabet explanation is sound: inflection would destroy the spelling unless the letter is coordinated or adjectival.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r14.anchor: قال لم تعرب حروف المعجم لأنك إنما أردت تعليم الهجاء قال أبو جعفر وهذا قول صحيح

NAHHAS:v5p3/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r15.claim: Distinct nūn follows the pause convention for alphabet letters; its distance from wāw supports clarity, while al-Kisāʾī assimilates it to nearby ṣād in كهيعص.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r15.anchor: ومن بين النون قال سبيل حروف الهجاء أن يوقف عليها وأيضا فإن النون بعيدة المخرج من الواو

NAHHAS:v5p3/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r16.claim: One assimilation avoids disturbing Nun's written form; without nasalization, the assimilated letter takes the status of its counterpart.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r16.anchor: ومن أدغم بغتة أراد ألا يزل رسم النون ومن حذف الغنة قال المدغم قد صار حكمه حكم ما أدغم فيه

NAHHAS:v5p3/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r17.speaker: أبو حاتم
NAHHAS:v5p3/r17.claim: The kasra reading resolves two successive vowelless sounds.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r17.anchor: ومن قرأ ( نون والقلم ) كسر لالتقاء الساكنين قال أبو حاتم

NAHHAS:v5p3/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r18.claim: The letter-name plural is نونات; the fish-name has نينان for many and أنوان for few, and نونة is also possible.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r18.anchor: وإن جمعت نون قلت نونات على أنه حرف هجاء فإن جمعته على أنه اسم للحوت قلت في الجمع الكثير نينان

NAHHAS:v5p3/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r19.claim: The oath is by the writing pen; tradition identifies it as the pen that wrote the Preserved Tablet's contents through Resurrection.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r19.anchor: القلم ) خفض بواو القسم وهو القلم الذي يكتب به غير أن التوقيف جاء أنه القلم

NAHHAS:v5p3/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p3/r20.claim: Reports through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra attribute the Preserved Tablet account to Ibn ʿAbbās and a Prophetic report.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r20.anchor: روى ذلك القاسم بن أبي بزة عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس ومعاوية بن قرة عن أبيه يرفعه

NAHHAS:v5p3/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p3/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p3/r21.claim: The wāw is conjunction, not another oath; ما with its verb is verbal noun or relative pronoun, and the oath's response is the next verse.
NAHHAS:v5p3/r21.anchor: وما يسطرون ) واو عطف لا واو قسم وما والفعل مصدر ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى الذي

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r1.claim: The oath answer is the following negative clause, as in ص والقرآن.

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r2.speaker: قوم
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r2.claim: One group identifies ن as a fish, one of the fish.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r2.anchor: وزعم قوم أنه اسم لحوت وأنه واحد النينان

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r3.speaker: قوم
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r3.claim: Another group identifies ن as an inkpot.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r3.anchor: وقوم أنه اسم الدواة، وقوم أنه اسم لوح

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r4.speaker: قوم
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r4.claim: Another group identifies ن as a written tablet.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r4.anchor: وقوم أنه اسم لوح مكتوب فيه

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī challenges the inkpot and fish glosses for lacking a defensible case ending and role in the oath syntax.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وأما قولهم هو الدواة فما أدري: أهو وضع لغوي أم شرعي

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r6.claim: The author praises Zamakhsharī’s objection as an especially strong achievement of grammatical analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r6.anchor: وهذا الذي أورده أبو القاسم من محاسن علم الإعراب، وقل من يتقنه.

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r7.claim: The common reading has silent nūn; Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim assimilate it into wāw, Warsh varies, and others pronounce it clearly.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r7.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " ن " ساكن النون كنظائره. وأدغم ابن عامر والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r8.claim: Reports differ on whether those who assimilate nūn use ghunna.

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-Sammāl, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read kasra; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿĪsā sometimes read fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن وأبو السمال وابن أبي إسحاق بكسر النون وسعيد بن جبير وعيسى بخلاف عنه بفتحها

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r10.claim: Kasra is attributed to meeting two quiescent consonants; it cannot be genitive from an omitted oath preposition, unusual beyond the divine name and requiring tanwin.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r10.anchor: فالأولى على التقاء الساكنين. ولا يجوز أن يكون مجرورا على القسم، حذف حرف الجر وبقي علمه

SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r11.claim: Fatḥa may mark a built form chosen for lightness, or genitive under an omitted oath preposition in a weak dialect, as in فالحق والحق.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1/r11.anchor: وأما الفتح فيحتمل ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أن يكون بناء، وأوثر على الأصل للخفة

SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r1.claim: An unnamed poetic line فذاك أمانة الله الثريد exemplifies accusative after omitting the oath preposition.

SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r2.claim: ما may be relative or a particle, meaning what scribes or angelic recorders write; its pronoun is inferred from context and the writing instrument.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r2.anchor: ما " موصولة اسمية أو حرفية، أي: والذي يسطرونه من الكتب، وهم: الكتاب أو الحفظة من الملائكة

SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows القلم to stand for its users, making يسطرون refer to them, like the implied possessor of الظلمات in 24:40.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن يراد بالقلم أصحابه، فيكون الضمير في " يسطرون " لهم

SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r4.claim: The author prefers the accusative after an omitted oath preposition because والقلم coordinates with its syntactic position.
SAMIN-DURR:68:1#2/r4.anchor: ومنع الصرف لما تقدم، وهذا أحسن لعطف " والقلم " على محله.

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r1.claim: The opening is read either by assimilating nūn into wāw, by articulating the nūn distinctly before wāw, or as Nūn with fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r1.anchor: قرئت بإدغام النون في الواو، وقرئت بتبيين النون عند الواو

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r2.claim: Zajjāj prefers assimilation into wāw whether wāw is still or vowelled, since the exegetical accounts distinguish the opening from a bare letter-name; assimilation can occur with nūn open.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r2.anchor: والذي اختار إدغام النون في الواو كانت الواو ساكنة أو متحركة

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r3.claim: One exegetical account identifies Nūn as the fish on which the seven earths were spread.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r3.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن " نون " الحوت التي دحيت عليها سبع الأرضين

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r4.claim: Another exegetical account identifies nūn as an inkpot; the source says the accounts do not interpret it as one of the alphabetic letter names.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r4.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أيضا أن النون الدواة، ولم يجئ في التفسير كما فسرت حروف الهجاء

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r5.claim: A vowelless nūn is possible only if it is treated as a letter name, which is why that reading does not fit the other exegetical interpretations.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r5.anchor: والإسكان لا يجوز أن يكون فيه إلا حرف هجاء

ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r6.claim: A report says the Pen was the first creation; God commanded it to write the decree, and it recorded what would happen until the Resurrection, including the fate of Abū Lahab.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203/r6.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن أول ما خلق الله القلم، فقال له: اكتب، فقال:

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r1.claim: What is written refers to what the angels write.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: (وما يسطرون). معناه: وما تكتب الملائكة

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r1.claim: This is chronologically the first occurrence of the disjointed letters that precede some Qur'anic surahs; Asad points to Appendix II for theories about them.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r1.anchor: Chronologically, this is the first appearance of any of the "disjointed" [i.e., single] letters

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r2.claim: Some early commentators cited by Tabari take nun as an abbreviation for a homonymous noun meaning great fish or inkwell; Asad rejects this on the grammatical grounds advanced by Zamakhshari and Razi.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n1/r2.anchor: the letter n, pronounced nun, represents here an abbreviation of the identically-pronounced noun which signifies both "great fish" and "inkwell"

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad points to 74:32, note 23, for the meaning of the oath particle wa.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r1.anchor: For the meaning of the adjurative particle wa at the beginning of this sentence, see first half of note 23 on 74:32.

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r2.claim: The pen recalls the first revelation, 96:1-5, and thereby emphasizes Muhammad's prophethood.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r2.anchor: The mention of "the pen" is meant to recall the earliest Qur'anic revelation, namely, the first five verses of surah 96

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r3.claim: For the pen's symbolic significance, Asad directs readers to 96:3-5 and note 3.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n2/r3.anchor: As regards the symbolic significance of the concept of "the pen", see 96:3-5 and the corresponding note 3.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r1.claim: One proposed rule is that each disjoint letter uniquely suits its sūra; replacing nūn with qāf in this opening would violate that fit.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r1.anchor: لكل سورة منها ألا يناسبها غير الواردة فيها. فلو وضع (ق) في موضع (ن) لم يكن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r2.claim: The proposed rationale for opening Qāf with qāf is the repeated qāf vocabulary there, spanning revelation, creation, resurrection, and other themes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r2.anchor: وسورة ق بدئت به لما تكرر فيها من الكلمات بلفظ القاف، من ذكر: القرآن، والخلق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r3.claim: Another proposed rationale says Sūrat Nūn has matching endings and many nūn words.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r3.anchor: فواصلها كلها على هذا الوزن، مع ما تضمنت من الألفاظ النونية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r4.claim: The author finds the rhyme explanation unclear and notes that Sūrat al-Qalam’s endings include many words without the claimed nūn pattern.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r4.anchor: ولا أدري ما وجهه، وفي فواصل سورة القلم: عظيم، الخرطوم، زعيم، مكظوم، مذموم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r5.speaker: الزركشي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r5.claim: A symbolic reading says alif-lām-mīm spans the throat, tongue, and lips, signifying creation, resurrection, and worldly life with its laws.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r5.anchor: عمد الزركشي إلى التأويل والتخريج، حتى خرج بها إلى إشاريات بعيدة من مثل قولها: "و (الم) جمعت المخارج الثلاثة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r6.speaker: الزركشي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r6.claim: A symbolic reading says alif-lām-mīm-sād adds ṣād because al-Aʿrāf recounts prophetic stories and mentions distress in the Prophet’s breast.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r6.anchor: وسورة الأعراف زيد فيها الصاد على (الم) - المص - لما فيها من شرح القصص

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r7.claim: Some interpreters turn alif-lām-mīm-sād into the phrase alam nashraḥ laka ṣadrak.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p149/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال بعضهم، معنى (المص) : {أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r1.claim: The author says the proposed pattern also applies to Sūrat al-Rūm, whose closing verses defend the Qur’an against deniers and call the Prophet to patience.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r1.anchor: وكذلك يطرد الملحظ لا يتخلف، في سورة الروم، وفي ختامها تأتي هذه الآيات احتجاجاً للقرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r2.claim: She proposes surveying every letter-opening sūra in revelation order to find a shared rationale grounded in context, the circumstances of the mission, and the challenge of the miracle.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r2.anchor: استقراء كامل لجميع السور المفتتحة بالحروف المقطعة، مرتبة على حسب النزول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r3.claim: Sūrat al-Qalam is the first sūra opened by a disjoint letter and, on the well-known chronology, the second sūra revealed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r3.anchor: وأول سورة نزلت مفتتحة بالحرف، هي سورة القلم ثاني السور على المشهور في ترتيب النزول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r4.claim: The opening pairs nūn with the pen and writing, then answers those disputing the Qur’an’s miraculous character.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p160/r4.anchor: واللافت اقتران الحرف فيها بالقلم وما يسطرون، والرد على المجادلون في المعجزة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.claim: The opening verses affirm the Prophet’s mission and steady him against deniers who dispute the miracle and claim the Qur’an is merely tales of the ancients.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.anchor: واضح أن الآيات موجهه إلى تأييد نبوة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، تثبيت قلبه في مواجهة من يكذبونه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r3.claim: The deniers knew the old tales they invoked; some wrote them down and recited from them to challenge the Prophet.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r3.anchor: وإنهم لعلى علم بتلك الأساطير، وفيهم من كان يكتبها ويتلو منها تحدياً للمصطفى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r4.claim: The Qur’an’s miraculous verses are presented in the disbelievers’ own language and letters for comparison with their writings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r4.anchor: وهذه هي آيات المعجزة معروضة عليهم بلغتهم وحروفهم، فليقابلوها على ما لديهم مما كانوا يسطرون

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.claim: The author dates the dispute over the miracle to the earliest mission, when only the first verses of al-ʿAlaq had been revealed; nūn then signals the secret of the Qur’an’s miraculous expression.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.anchor: ولم يكن قد نزل من القرآن غير الآيات الأولى من سورة العلق. ومجئ الحرف (ن) في سورة القلم المكية المبكرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.claim: Al-Tur opens with a much longer oath than al-Qalam, whose oath is only by the pen and what is written; this broader setting suits the added accusation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.anchor: توسع في القسم في أول سورة الطور بخلاف سورة القلم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.claim: The extended opening oath in al-Tur makes its added denial of soothsaying fitting, unlike al-Qalam's brief oath by the pen and writing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.anchor: فناسب التوسع في الطور هذه الزيادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r1.claim: Tasṭir means writing; unlike kataba, which may be only a letter, two letters, or a word, satar implies a larger amount of writing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r1.anchor: يسطر أي يكتب والفرق بين سطر وكتب أن الكتابة قد تكون حرفاً واحداً أو حرفين أو كلمة أما السطر فالكتابة أكثر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r2.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r2.claim: Grammarians treat the phrase as one oath: the pen is sworn by, and what they write is coordinated to the oath and inherits its force; N is a disconnected letter like Qaf.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r2.anchor: النحاة يرون أنه قسم واحد ونعطف عليه وليس قسماً مستقلاً

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r3.claim: The coordinated phrase what they write shares the oath's syntactic and semantic status, just as coordinated sentence parts share their grammatical role.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r3.anchor: المعطوف على الشيء له حكمه فالمعطوف على المبتدأ مبتدأ والمعطوف على الخبر خبر والمعطوف على الفاعل فاعل فالحكم واحد والإخبار عنهم واحد.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r4.claim: Waw and fa can coordinate additional oath objects to the first oath even though fa itself is not an oath particle, as in the sequence of al-Naziat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1076/r4.anchor: ثم جاء بالفاء وهي ليست حرف قسم وإنما حرف عطف

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r1.claim: These readers make the final nūn of the letter name clear before wāw.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة: نون والقلم [1] النون في آخر الهجاء من نون ظاهرة عند الواو

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r2.speaker: الكسائي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r2.claim: Al-Kisai's transmission from Abu Bakr from Asim does not make the nūn clear in يس, نون, and طسم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r2.anchor: وروى الكسائي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم أنه كان لا يبين النون في يس ونون* وطسم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم وحسين عن أبي بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r3.claim: Hafs from Asim and Husayn from Abu Bakr are reported to make the nūn clear in نون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r3.anchor: وروى حفص عن عاصم وحسين عن أبي بكر أنه كان يبين النون في نون*

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r4.speaker: يعقوب عن نافع والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r4.claim: Yaqub from Nafi conceals the nūn; al-Kisai also does not make it clear in نون.
