FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r4.anchor: وروى يعقوب عن نافع أنه أخفاها، وكان الكسائي لا يبين النون في نون*

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r5.speaker: يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r5.claim: Yahya's report from Abu Bakr from Asim calls نون jazm, which indicates that he makes it clear.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r5.anchor: وقال يحيى عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: نون* جزم على هذا، وهذا يدل على أنه يبين

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r6.speaker: الحلواني عن قالون عن نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r6.claim: Al-Hilwani from Qalun from Nafi conceals the nūn in يس but makes it clear in نون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r6.anchor: الحلواني عن قالون عن نافع: يس مخفاة النون، ونون* ظاهرة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r7.claim: Clarity follows if the isolated letter name is treated as stopped and separate from what follows; concealment follows if it is connected, as indicated by hamzat al-wasl examples.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: وجه إظهار هذه النونات أنها من حروف ينوى بها الوقف، وإذا كانت موقوفة بدلالة اجتماع الساكنين

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r8.claim: Because the nūn is concealed only before mouth-letters, it is hidden when the name is connected to what follows.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p309/r8.anchor: وإذا وصلتها أخفيت النون معها، وقد بين ذلك فيما تقدم.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p350#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p350#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p350#2/r2.claim: Nūn and the following wāw are read with assimilation or clear pronunciation; the author refers to the earlier discussion in Yā Sīn.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p350#2/r2.anchor: يقرأ بالإدغام والإظهار وقد تقدم ذكر علله في يس

NASHR:v1p318/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p318/r1.speaker: أهل الأداء
NASHR:v1p318/r1.claim: Readers agree on a minimum length for madd before a quiescent letter, but differ in naming it: specialists call it full saturation, most call it enabling the madd, and some place it below hamza-lengthening.
NASHR:v1p318/r1.anchor: المحققون منهم على أنه الإشباع، والأكثرون على إطلاق تمكين المد فيه، وقال بعضهم: هو دون ما مد للهمز

NASHR:v1p318/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p318/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني وأبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p318/r2.claim: Many authorities, including Abu Hatim, Ibn Mujahid through al-Shadhāʾī, Makki, Ibn Shurayḥ, and al-Dānī, favor stronger madd for assimilated letters than pronounced ones because sound continues through assimilation; the dāl in dābba likewise exceeds muḥyāy for those who make it silent.
NASHR:v1p318/r2.anchor: فذهب كثير إلى أن مد المدغم منه أشبع تمكينا من المظهر من أجل الإدغام، لاتصال الصوت فيه وانقطاعه في المظهر

NASHR:v1p318/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p318/r3.speaker: أبو العز
NASHR:v1p318/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿIzz records the opposite ranking: madd in a pronounced, non-assimilated letter exceeds madd in an assimilated letter because the assimilated letter is strengthened by the following letter and its vowel.
NASHR:v1p318/r3.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى عكس ذلك، وهو أن المد في غير المدغم فوق المدغم

NASHR:v1p318/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p318/r4.speaker: جمهور القراء وأبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p318/r4.claim: The majority, including most of al-Dānī's teachers in Baghdad and Egypt, equalize madd for assimilated and pronounced letters: both involve two adjacent quiescent letters, the cause of madd.
NASHR:v1p318/r4.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى التسوية بين مد المدغم والمظهر في ذلك كله؛ إذ الموجب للمد هو التقاء الساكنين

NASHR:v2p18/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r1.speaker: الجمهور وأبو بكر عن عاصم
NASHR:v2p18/r1.claim: For ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr, most authorities give assimilation via Yaḥyā ibn Ādam and clear pronunciation via al-ʿAlīmī, though Iraqi transmitters also report clarity via Yaḥyā; both are sound on both routes, and both also occur through Ḥafṣ via ʿAmr.
NASHR:v2p18/r1.anchor: وأما عاصم فقطع له الجمهور بالإدغام من رواية أبي بكر من طريق يحيى بن آدم، وبالإظهار من طريق العليمي

NASHR:v2p18/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو جعفر وقنبل
NASHR:v2p18/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Abū Jaʿfar, and Qunbul read with clear pronunciation as their sole face in the preceding assimilation discussion.
NASHR:v2p18/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالإظهار وجها واحدا وهم أبو عمرو، وحمزة، وأبو جعفر وقنبل

NASHR:v2p18/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r3.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب وخلف وهشام
NASHR:v2p18/r3.claim: For the nūn in the opening nūn wāw of Nūn wa-l-qalam, as in Yā-Sīn wa-l-Qurʾān, al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb, Khalaf, and Hishām assimilate; Qālūn consistently pronounces clearly.
NASHR:v2p18/r3.anchor: النون في الواو من ن والقلم والخلاف فيه كالخلاف في يس والقرآن أدغم النون في الواو الكسائي ويعقوب وخلف وهشام

NASHR:v2p18/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r4.speaker: ورش
NASHR:v2p18/r4.claim: Reports differ for Warsh: al-Azraq's route gives assimilation in al-Tajrīd and other works, while al-Tadhkira and al-ʿUnwān give clarity; al-Hidāya calls clarity correct, al-Taysīr says it is general practice, and Ibn Shurayḥ, al-Shāṭibī and Makki allow both.
NASHR:v2p18/r4.anchor: ورش، فقطع له بالإدغام من طريق الأزرق

NASHR:v2p18/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r5.speaker: ورش وعاصم والبزي وابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p18/r5.claim: For ʿĀṣim, al-Bazzī, and Ibn Dhakwān, the route-based disagreement follows Yā-Sīn, except Sibt al-Khayyāṭ uniquely records Abū Bakr through al-ʿAlīmī assimilating here but pronouncing clearly there.
NASHR:v2p18/r5.anchor: وأما عاصم والبزي وابن ذكوان فالخلاف عنهم كالخلاف في يس من الطرق المذكورة إلا أن سبط الخياط قطع في كفايته

NASHR:v2p18/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو جعفر وقالون وقنبل
NASHR:v2p18/r6.claim: All remaining readers pronounce the nūn of Nūn wa-l-qalam clearly.
NASHR:v2p18/r6.anchor: وأظهر النون من ن الباقون وهم أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو جعفر وقالون وقنبل

NASHR:v2p18/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p18/r7.speaker: حمزة وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p18/r7.claim: At the nūn before mīm in Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm at the openings of al-Shuʿarāʾ and al-Qaṣaṣ, Ḥamza and Abū Jaʿfar pronounce clearly and the others assimilate; Abū Jaʿfar's pause on disjoint letters entails clarity in these other initials too.
NASHR:v2p18/r7.anchor: النون عند الميم من طسم أول الشعراء والقصص فأظهر النون عندها حمزة وأبو جعفر. والباقون بالإدغام

QIRAAT-ER:68:1:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:68:1:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:68:1:1#1/r1.claim: Assimilation merges the final nūn into wāw incompletely, carrying its nasal into the oath particle.
QIRAAT-ER:68:1:1#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of nūn's final consonant into the wāw — idghām nāqiṣ, merging the nasal

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r1.speaker: قتادة والحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r1.claim: Qatāda and al-Hasan gloss what is written as what people write.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r1.anchor: عن وقتادة الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ ن والقلم وما يسطرون ﴾ وما يكتبون

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the Pen and commanded it to write destiny through the events of that day until the Hour; after the book was folded and the Pen lifted, water vapor rose and the heavens split, then the fish Nun was created beneath the earth, whose movement made earth sway until mountains were fixed in it. He recited through 68:2.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307/r2.anchor: عن الأعمش عن أبي ظبيان عن ابن عباس قال إن أول ما خلق الله من شيء خلق القلم فقال اكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r1.claim: At pause ن is read with sukūn; most readers keep it still and assimilate it into wāw, with some nasalizing and others not, while other readers use kasra or fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r1.anchor: بالسكون على الوقف وقرأ الأكثرون بسكون النون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Isa (in one transmission) read fatḥa; it may mark two meeting sukūns, or an elided oath particle in a genitive construction, or an elided imperative such as اذكر with نصب rather than fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بخلاف عنه بفتحها وكل لالتقاء الساكنين وجوز أن يكون الفتح بإضمار حرف القسم في موضع الجر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r3.claim: If ن is the surah’s name, its case may be explained as accusative after an implied verb or nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject; it is indeclinable as a feminine proper name.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r3.anchor: وامتناع الصرف للتعريف والتأنيث على أنه علم للسورة ثم إن جعل اسما للحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r4.speaker: السلف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r4.claim: The early authorities regard ن as one of the ambiguous verses; many later scholars instead take it to be a letter name, supported by its written form and lack of ordinary inflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r4.anchor: واختار السلف إن ن من المتشابه وغير واحد من الخلف أنه هنا من أسماء الحروف وقالوا يؤيد ذلك أنه لو كان اسم جنس أو علما لأعرب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r5.claim: A report authenticated by al-Diya and al-Hakim says God created the fish called اليهموت, spread the earth on it, and steadied the trembling earth with mountains; Ibn Abbas then recited the verse. Mujahid also reports the fish interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r5.anchor: ففي حديث رواه الضياء والحاكم وصححه وجمع عن ابن عباس خلق الله تعالى النون فبسطت الأرض عليه فاضطرب النون فمادت الأرض فأثبتت بالجبال

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak also say ن means an inkpot.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أيضا والحسن وقتادة والضحاك أنه اسم للدواة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari denies that ن meaning an inkpot is established in recognized Arabic; Ibn Atiyya allows a dialectal or Arabized foreign usage and cites a disputed poem.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23/r7.anchor: وأنكر الزمخشري ورود النون بمعنى الدواة في اللغة أو في الاستعمال المعتد به وقال ابن عطية يحتمل أن يكون لغة لبعض العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r1.claim: Some interpret the Pen as the one that wrote all that will happen until Judgment in the Preserved Tablet; others take it as the pens of the noble recording angels. On both readings أل is referential.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r1.anchor: والأولون منهم من فسر القلم بالذي خط في اللوح المحفوظ ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة ومنهم من فسره بقلم الملائكة الكرام الكاتبين وأل فيه على التفسيرين للعهد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r2.claim: Others understand the Pen generically; a few return to the earlier interpretations, though their inkpot seems to be a special one created when the Pen was created.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r2.anchor: والآخرون منهم من فسره بالجنس على أن التعريف فيه جنسي ومنهم وهم قليل من فسره بما تقدم أيضا لكن الظاهر من كلامهم أن الدواة ليست عبارة عن الدواة المعروفة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r3.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r3.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says ن is a tablet of light and the Pen a pen of light, writing what will occur until Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r3.anchor: وعن معاوية بن قرة يرفعه أن ن لوح من نور والقلم قلم من نور يجري بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r4.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r4.claim: Ja‘far al-Sadiq identifies ن as a river among the rivers of Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r4.anchor: وعن جعفر الصادق أنه نهر من أنهار الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r5.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r5.claim: Al-Bahr says none of the proposed meanings of ن is sound except that it is a letter name; al-Alusi questions whether this accounts for al-Hakim’s authentication and the weight of al-Diya’s collection, while noting the many conflicting reports from Ibn Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r5.anchor: وفي البحر لعله لا يصح شيء من ذلك أي من جميع ما ذكر في ن ما عدا كونه اسما من أسماء الحروف وكأنه إن كان مطلعا على الروايات التي ذكرناها لم يعتبر تصحيح الحاكم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi finds the fish or river readings syntactically awkward and the inkpot reading poorly attested; the Qamus alone does not establish it, Ibn Atiyya’s verse is unverified, and the proposed fish-to-ink metaphor is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r6.anchor: وكونه بمعنى الحوت أطلق على الدواة مجازا بعلاقة المشابهة فإن بعض الحيتان يستخرج منه شيء أشد سوادا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi dismisses the storytellers’ reports about this passage as unreliable and says they should not be heeded.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r7.anchor: وللقصاص هذا الفصل روايات لا يعول عليها ولا ينبغي الإصغاء إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r8.claim: The Pen deserves the oath if it is the first-created Tablet Pen or the angels’ pens; ordinary human pens also merit honor for their many benefits, especially recording God’s books.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p23#2/r8.anchor: وأما استحقاق ما في أيدي الناس إذا أريد به الجنس لذلك فلكثرة منافعه ولو لم يكن له مزية سوى كونه آلة لتحرير كتب الله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r1.claim: The pronoun may refer to the singular Tablet Pen, pluralized honorifically, or to writing instruments generally, plural because they are many; in the latter case writing is attributed to the tool metonymically and it stands for its rational users.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r1.anchor: أما للقلم مرادا به قلم اللوح وعبر عنه بضمير الجمع تعظيما له أو له مرادا به جنس ما به الخط فضمير الجمع لتعدده لكنه ليس بكاتب حقيقة بل هو آلة للكاتب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the scribes or recorders implied by the Pen, or to the Pen’s owners by metonymy or an omitted possessive construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r2.anchor: أو للكتبة أو الحفظة المفهومين من القلم أولهم باعتبار أنه أريد بالقلم أصحابه تجوزا أو بتقدير مضاف معه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r3.claim: Taking ما to mean من is an awkward forced reading; it is more naturally relative, meaning what they write, or a verbal noun, meaning their writing.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24/r3.anchor: وأما كونه لما وهي بمعنى من فتكلف بارد والظاهر فيها أنها إما موصولة أي والذي يسطرونه أو مصدرية أي وسطرهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r1.claim: They identify Nūn as the great fish on whose back the earth rests.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: هو الحوت الذي على ظهره الأرض. وهو قول مجاهد ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي ظبيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God first created the Pen, which wrote all events until Judgment Day; then Nūn bore the spread earth, trembled, and the mountains were set to stabilize it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r2.anchor: وروى أبو ظبيان عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم، فجرى بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة، ثم خلق النون فبسط الأرض على ظهره فتحرك النون فمادت الأرض، فأثبتت بالجبال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil name the fish Yamhūt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r3.anchor: واختلفوا في اسمه، فقال الكلبي ومقاتل: [اسمه] (4) يهموت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r7.speaker: الرواة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r7.claim: Unnamed narrators say an angel carries the earths; a 40,000-horned, 40,000-legged bull stands on a 500-year-thick ruby; a rock as thick as seven heavens and earths rests on Nūn over sea, wind, and divine Power; the bull's breaths cause tides.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r7.anchor: وقالت الرواة: لما خلق الله الأرض وفتقها بعث من تحت العرش ملكا فهبط إلى الأرض حتى دخل تحت الأرضين السبع فوضعها على عاتقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r8.claim: The rock in this account is the one mentioned in Luqmān 31:16.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r8.anchor: وهي الصخرة التي قال لقمان لابنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r9.claim: Another saying reduces the whole world and all it contains to two letters: God's command Be, and it was.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p182#2/r9.anchor: يقال: فكل الدنيا كلها بما عليها حرفان قال لها الجبار:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r1.claim: The Pen is the luminous pen with which God wrote the Reminder, and its length is the distance between heaven and earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r1.anchor: {والقلم} [هو] (2) الذي كتب الله به الذكر، وهو قلم من نور طوله ما بين السماء والأرض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r2.claim: Another report says the Pen was the first thing created; it split in two, then was commanded to write all events until the Resurrection on the Preserved Tablet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r2.anchor: ويقال: أول ما خلق الله القلم ونظر إليه فانشق بنصفين، ثم قال: اجر بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة فجرى على اللوح المحفوظ بذلك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r3.claim: What they write is the record of human deeds written by the guardian angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187/r3.anchor: {وما يسطرون} يكتبون أي ما تكتب الملائكة الحفظة من أعمال بني آدم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan and has fifty-two verses.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r2.claim: Nūn is a letter name; alternatives identify it as a whale, the great fish that bears the earth, or an inkwell made from a whale product darker than lampblack.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r2.anchor: من أسماء الحروف، وقيل اسم الحوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r3.claim: Other explanations identify nūn as the great fish that bears the earth or as an inkwell made from a whale product darker than lampblack.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r3.anchor: أو البهموت وهو الذي عليه الأرض، أو الدواة

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r4.claim: The letter-name explanation is supported by nūn's quiescent form and written shape.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r4.anchor: ويؤيد الأول سكونه وكتبه بصورة الحرف

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb conceal nūn, treating the separated wāw like a connected one; a similar transmission is reported from Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r5.anchor: وأخفى ابن عامر والكسائي ويعقوب النون

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r6.claim: Nūn is also read with fatḥa or kasra, as Ṣād is.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r7.claim: The Pen may be the one that inscribed the Preserved Tablet or the instrument used for writing; God swears by it because of its many benefits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r7.anchor: وهو الذي خط اللوح، أو الذي يخط به

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r8.claim: The phrase means what is written; the pronoun may refer to the Pen, its writers, scribes, or guardian angels, and mā may be a verbal noun or relative pronoun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r8.anchor: والضمير ل { القلم } بالمعنى الأول على التعظيم

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r9.claim: If the Pen is intended as a genus, writing is attributed to instruments and treated like the act of rational beings because an instrument stands in for them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:1/r9.anchor: وإسناد الفعل إلى الأدلة وإجراؤه مجرى أولي العلم

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r2.claim: Because the muṣḥaf writes N as one letter, Bint al-Shati sets aside al-Ṭabarī's views that it means a fish, a tablet of light, or an inkwell: those nouns would be written with three letters.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r2.anchor: يجعلنا نستبعد ابتداء ما نقل الإمام الطبري من اختلاف أهل التأويل فيه

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r3.claim: A report identifies N with the fish beneath the seventh earth that bears the earths; it was created before heaven and earth, and the earth's movement was steadied by mountains.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r3.anchor: عن "ابن عباس ومجاهد" في هذا الحوت الذي عليه الأرضون، تحت الأرض السابعة

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī admits uncertainty about whether “inkwell” is a linguistic or revealed term, a common noun or a proper name, and whether it is diptote.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r4.anchor: وقد صرح الزمخشري بأنه لا يدري - ولا أدري معه - "أهو وضع لغوي أم شرعي؟

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r5.speaker: قول آخر
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r5.claim: Another view makes N the name of the sura; Bint al-Shati finds this unhelpful because the sura would simply be named after its opening letter, as Ṣād and Qāf are.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r5.anchor: وفي قول آخر إن (ن) اسم للسورة. وليس فذ هذا القول ما يغني

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r6.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib reads N as the familiar letter of the Arabic alphabet, the interpretation Bint al-Shati finds reassuring.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r6.anchor: ويبدو أن الراغب الأصفهاني، اختار أن تكون

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r1.claim: Al-Qalam is the first sura to open with a disjoined letter; Bint al-Shati says 28 more followed, 26 Meccan and three from the early Medinan period.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r1.anchor: من هذه الحروف المقطعة بفواتح السور، وبعدها نزلت ثمان وعشرون سورة مفتتحة بهذه الحروف

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r2.claim: The disjoined letters comprise fourteen distinct letters, half the letters of the Arabic alphabet.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r2.anchor: ومجموع حروفها بغير المكرر منها أربعة حرفاً، هي نصف حروف معجمنا.

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r3.speaker: أصحاب هذا القول
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r3.claim: One view treats the letters as signs for divine names or attributes, but its adherents do not agree on expansions: N may stand for Helper or Light, for example.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r3.anchor: وأصحاب هذا القول لا يكادون يجمعون على دلالات الحروف فيه،

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r4.speaker: قول
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r4.claim: A view calls the letters marks made by the revelation scribes; Bint al-Shati objects that human marks would then occur inside Qur'anic verses after the basmala.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r4.anchor: وقيل هي علامات وضعها كتاب الوحي. ويمنعه أن تدخل هذه العلامات، وهي من قول البشر

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r5.speaker: حيى بن أخطب
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r5.claim: The abjad theory is identified as an Isrāʾīliyyāt report: Huyayy calculates the letters in alif-lām-mīm as 71 years, then alif-lām-mīm-ṣād as 161 and alif-lām-rāʾ as 271, and questions whether to follow a prophet with that term; the Prophet replies with further letters, leaving the Jews unsure of the term.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r5.anchor: وهذا من إسرائيليات "حيى بن أخطب اليهودي" فتقول الراوية إن أخاه أبا ياسر مر في رجال من يهود

BINTSHATI:v2p41/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r6.speaker: قول
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r6.claim: Another view makes the letters alerts to what follows, often a mention of the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI:v2p41/r6.anchor: وأكثر ما يكون بعدها ذكر القرآن الكريم

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī and Ibn al-Qayyim elaborate the view that the opening letters alert readers to what follows, and Ibn Kathīr surveys its occurrences.

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r2.speaker: الشعبي
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r2.claim: The letters are among the ambiguous matters whose knowledge God reserves; al-Shaʿbī says every book has a secret and the Qur'an's secret is its opening letters.
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r2.anchor: ما روى عن الشعبي أنه سئل عن فواتح السور: إن لكل كتاب سراً وإن سر هذا القرآن فواتح السور.

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r3.speaker: ابن القيم
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says the letters honor the alphabet as the building blocks of God's speech and revealed books, and as a gift that enables people to speak.
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r3.anchor: واختار ابن القيم أن يكون في افتتاح السور بها، تنبيه على شرف الحروف وعظم قدرها وجلالتها

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r4.claim: Bint al-Shati finds a still closer explanation in the letters showing that the Qur'an is made from the same letters familiar to its Arabic audience, exposing their inability to produce its like.
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r4.anchor: وأقرب منه قول من قالوا إن هذه الحروف

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r5.claim: In this early Meccan sura, N draws attention to the mystery of the letter in the Qur'an's inimitable eloquence.
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r5.anchor: ومجيء الحرف (ن) في (سورة القلم) المكية المبكرة، فيه لفت واضح إلى سر الحرف في البيان المعجز.

BINTSHATI:v2p42/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r6.claim: Because the sura answers pagans who deny the Prophet and call the Qur'an old legends, its opening prepares the challenge to produce its like and brings them to confront the proof in their own language and letters.
BINTSHATI:v2p42/r6.anchor: فكأن هذه تمهيد للمعاجزة التي تتحداهم أن يأتوا بمثله، واستدراجهم إلى أن تلزمهم الحجة

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r1.claim: The first revealed word, “Read,” points to God's great sign in creating humans from a clinging form and teaching by the pen; Al-Qalam then opens with N to point to letters as the basis of reading, knowledge, and eloquence.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r1.anchor: وقد كانت كلمة الوحي الأولى "اقرأ" لافته إلى آية الله الكبرى، في الإنسان الذي خلقه سبحانه من علق

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r2.claim: An isolated letter supplies no meaning and is nearly only a sound; its greater mystery appears when it takes its place in a word.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r2.anchor: تنطق به منفرداً منقطعاً فلا يعطي أي معنى أو دلالة، بل لا يكاد يخرج عن مجرد صوت

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r3.speaker: الإمام الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the oath is by the pen God created and commanded to write everything that will happen until the Resurrection.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r3.anchor: قال الإمام الطبري إن القلم معروف "غير أن الذي أقسم به ربنا من الأقلام، القلم الذي خلقه تعالى فأمره بكتابه

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r4.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r4.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim extols the pen as a sign and among God's first creations, by which decree and law were written, revelation and religion recorded, scripture established, knowledge preserved, and human affairs served.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r4.anchor: قال: "فأقسم بالكتاب - ن - وبالقلم الذي هو إحدى آياته وأول مخلوقاته

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r5.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r5.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim distinguishes twelve ranks of pens, with the pre-eternal pen of divine decree highest and most honored; the oath magnifies it.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r5.anchor: ثم عقد فصلاً في مراتب الأقلام فجعلها اثنى عشر قلماً، أعلاها وأجلها قدراً قلم القدر السابق

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r6.claim: This discussion points toward interpreting the pronoun as the recording angels, who write creatures' fates and deeds in the Preserved Tablet by God's command.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r6.anchor: بأن الضمير في الفعل للحفظة من الملائكة الذين يكتبون بأمر الله أقدار الخلائق وأعمالهم

BINTSHATI:v2p43/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r7.speaker: قول آخر
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r7.claim: Another view identifies the pen as the familiar writing implement, honored because God taught by the pen.
BINTSHATI:v2p43/r7.anchor: وفيه قول آخر، هو أنه القلم المألوف المعتاد الذي يسطر به الناس كتاباتهم

BINTSHATI:v2p44/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati takes the waw as an oath of exaltation, drawing attention to familiar writing and the letter's hidden power as a prelude to answering the pagans' argument.
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r1.anchor: الأول في القسم للتعظيم، لملحظ بياني، هو اللفت إلى ما عهدوا من أمر القلم والكتابة

BINTSHATI:v2p44/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r2.claim: She prefers to take “what they write” as the Arabs who copied ancient legends and tried to liken the Qur'an to them; the verb choice anticipates the accusation in 68:15.
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r2.anchor: والأقرب عندنا أن يكون الضمير في {يسطرون} لمن كانوا ينقلون من العرب أساطير القدماء

BINTSHATI:v2p44/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r3.claim: The accusation that the Qur'an is ancient legends recurs in the cited verses, where disbelievers claim it was copied, recited to the Prophet, or could be matched.
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r3.anchor: ونظيره ما في الآيات: {وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلاً}

BINTSHATI:v2p44/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports in the Sīra that some Arabs copied ancient legends and recited them to impugn the Prophet; Bint al-Shati invites comparison of those writings with the Qur'an in their language and letters.
BINTSHATI:v2p44/r4.anchor: على ما روى "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) . وهذه هي آيات الكتاب المعجز معروضة عليهم بلغتهم وحروفهم

BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.claim: The sūra’s closing words support the Prophet and link back to its opening, which likewise affirms his freedom from madness and his great character.
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.anchor: تأييداً للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، يرتبط بما بدأت به السورة من مثل هذا التأييد الإلهي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.claim: The sura follows al-Mulk’s contrast between the astray and guided and between bad and good action, then its closing image of life-giving water.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.anchor: في آخر ( الملك ) والمسيء والمحسن في العمل أولها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.claim: Al-Mulk’s closing water points to God’s power to restore life: none but the fully powerful can bring it back, and the One who revives bodies can revive dead spirits through knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.anchor: فكان قادرا على كل ما يريد , وكان لا يقدر على كل ما يريده إلا من كمل علمه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r3.claim: The knowledge bestowed on the unlettered Prophet demonstrates the breadth of divine power and knowledge; this sura opens with the named final letter of the previous sura’s closing phrase.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r3.anchor: دل على شمول قدرته بكمال علمه بما أفاده على النبي الكريم الأمي من العلوم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r4.claim: Nūn is an alphabet letter associated by its place in words for light, fire, growth, intelligence, purity, counsel, news, excellence, rescue, carving, and regret with manifestation and knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r4.anchor: هذه الكلمة حرف من حروف المعجم وهي اسم لمسمى به ظهور الأشياء وعلمها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r5.claim: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq is reported to have said every book has a secret and the Quran’s secret is these letters, known only to God; no grading is given.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه أنه قال : لكل كتاب سر وسر القرآن هذه الحروف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r6.claim: Nūn is shared in Arabic by the letter, inkpot, fish, and sword blade; its sukun first signals a letter but does not exclude the other senses, since Arabic can pause a word for emphasis.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r6.anchor: هذا الحرف مشتركا في اللغة بين حرف المعجم والدواة والحوت وشفرة السيف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r7.claim: Other proposed meanings include the tablet, the correct word, and a fish; these senses allow the letter’s encompassing reference to any element.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : النون اللوح , والنونة الكلمة من الصواب , والسمكة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r8.claim: Through ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās interprets nūn as the final letter of al-Raḥmān, the inkpot, and the cosmic fish al-Bahmūt; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r8.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه آخر حروف الرحمن والدواة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r9.claim: The oath may encompass the letter and pen, signifying comprehensive knowledge, or the sword and its momentous effects; all proposed referents point to encompassing power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r9.anchor: ويكون الإقسام وقع بالنون والقلم علوا للإحاطة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r10.claim: Whatever the intended sense, nūn signifies encompassing hidden realities whose results appear as decree and destiny, either misery or felicity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p89#2/r10.anchor: وكيفما كان المراد فهو الإحاطة , وهو سر باطن لا يظهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r1.claim: Nūn issues from a very open, easy, light articulation at the tongue tip and upper gum; nūn, lām, and rāʾ are liquid letters because edges are slippery.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r1.anchor: فغنه يخرج مما بين طرف اللسان وفويق الثنايا من اللثة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r2.claim: Among these letters, nūn has the firmest articulation where tongue and gum meet, and its name repeats its sound, ending where it began.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r2.anchor: والنون أمكنها في هذا المخرج وأشدها انطباقا فيما بين اللسان واللثة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r3.claim: The letter’s frame rests on the prominent, strong wāw, itself a liquid letter; liquid letters are light on the tongue and readily combine, unlike ṣāmitah letters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r3.anchor: واختص بكون عماده وقوامه الحرف الأقوى الأظهر ذا الرفعة والعلو وهو الواو الزلقية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r4.claim: Arabic words longer than three letters cannot consist only of ṣāmitah letters; at least one liquid letter must occur, while alif is outside both classes as unlocated breath.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r4.anchor: وأما المصمتة فمنعت أن تنفرد بنفسها في لغة العرب في كلمة هي أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r5.claim: Nūn’s open, light articulation and its voiced, open, low quality, between stop and fricative, with nasalization when quiescent, mirror knowledge’s breadth and penetration into hidden things.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r5.anchor: فقد ناسبت بمخرجها لسعته وخفته ووصفها بالزلاقة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r6.claim: Nūn shares nasalization with mīm, but is the original in nasalization and manifestation, matching knowledge’s priority and prominence.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r6.anchor: ويشاركه الميم في الغنة كما أنه يشاركه في أن له حظا من الظهور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r7.claim: As a letter that may be augmentative or original, nūn parallels knowledge: it expands when cultivated and contracts when neglected.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r7.anchor: وهو أيضا من حروف الذبذبة والزيادة التي لا تستقر على حال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r8.claim: Nūn can replace other letters but is not itself replaced, just as knowledge is foundational rather than subordinate to other things.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r8.anchor: وهو من حروف الأبدال التي تبدل من غيرها ولا يكون غيرها بدلا منها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r9.claim: As a sound, healthy consonant rather than a weak letter, nūn reflects the strength and solidity of knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r9.anchor: وهو من الحروف الصحيحة وليست معتلة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r10.claim: The author classifies nūn as a hidden, mixed letter and among oral ṣumm letters, defined by firm, established articulation; these qualities fit knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r10.anchor: وهو إذا كان مخفي من الحروف المشربة ويقال لها المخالطة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r11.claim: Nūn’s point of articulation and all its attributes correspond to knowledge, establishing knowledge as the sura’s central purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r11.anchor: فقد انطبقت بمخرجها وجميع صفاتها على العلم الذي هو مقصود السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r12.claim: The pen’s role in displaying and spreading knowledge and disclosing secrets is obvious to anyone with reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r12.anchor: وأما رتبة القلم في بيان العلم وإظهاره وكشف خفاياه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r13.claim: Nūn accompanies every letter through tanwīn; since vowel marks signal life, tanwīn after them signals knowledge that completes life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r13.anchor: أنه يصحب كل حرف لأن حده هو ما يعبر عنه التنوين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r14.claim: Nūn’s name stands for light and anything that reveals hidden things: knowledge, sun and moon, other lights, eyes, ink, and tools that make forms visible.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r14.anchor: ثم هو اسم لكل ما يظهر ما خفي باطنا كالعلم في الإدراك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r15.claim: The author extends nūn’s symbolism to plant growth and guidance, and to fire’s emergence from wood, iron, or stone and its return to ash.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r15.anchor: ( ومنه معنى النجم النباتي الذي هو للشجر بمنزلة الفول للبشر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r16.claim: Nūn applies to all kinds of manifestation, not one particular object; together with kāf, the sign of creation, it causes things to appear.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p90/r16.anchor: ولما كان هذا الحرف اسما لما به ظهور أمر لم يختص بشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r1.claim: The nūn and kāf in God’s command to a thing, Be, and it is, express the appearance of all things through divine creative power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r1.anchor: إنما قلنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن فيكون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets nūn as the inkpot from which the pen draws; this follows from the letter’s application to every manifestation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r2.anchor: ولصدقه على كل مظهر فسره ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما بالدواة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r3.claim: Nūn appears in words for high land and emergence, such as najd and a young woman’s breast, sharing the sense of manifestation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r3.anchor: وليلحظ موقعه في نجد فإنه اسم لما ارتفع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r4.claim: Other nūn words signify manifestation, including blowing, benefit, victory, piercing, digging, increase, and growth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r4.anchor: وفي النفخ والنفع والنصر والنقر والنقب وما أشبهها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r5.claim: Nūn is lofty, inward, and all-encompassing, supported by wāw and ending as it began; mīm is completed by a descending element and wāw’s alif supports its height.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r5.anchor: ولأجل علوه واستطبانه وأنه استغراق المظهر المبين كانت إقامته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r6.claim: Nūn, mīm, and wāw signify two worlds: the first nūn is the light of sight and the closing nūn the light of the heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r6.anchor: وهذه الحروف الثلاثة ظاهرة في عالمين ظاهرهما المبدوء به وباطنهما المختوم به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r7.claim: Because nūn lies in the tens, it marks a hidden, lower doubling of hāʾ; it is visible beside hidden hāʾ and hidden beside manifest mīm, making the prior sura’s kingdom manifest.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r7.anchor: فكان ظاهرا بالإضافة إلى خفاء الهاء باطنا بالإضافة إلى ظهور الميم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r8.claim: Every deed is completed through the light of knowledge, as outward signs depend on their hidden source; nūn is ink like the knowledge by which the pen reveals forms.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r8.anchor: ولذلك انبنى تمام كل عمل على نور علم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r9.claim: A report says the earth rests on a hidden cosmic fish called nūn, and people of Paradise first eat an extra portion of its liver together with the bull; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r9.anchor: ما بطن دون الأرض من النون الذي عليه الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r10.claim: The hidden nūn beneath the earth contrasts with the visible emerald Mount Qāf encircling the world; scholars rule hearts through knowledge, while kings rule bodies through power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r10.anchor: وقابل استبطان النون في الأرض ظهور القاف على ظاهرها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r11.claim: Scholars and kings are the two groups that exercise authority over people, one through knowledge and the other through power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r11.anchor: وهذان الصفنان من الخلق هما المستوليان على الناس

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r12.claim: Qāf and nūn are paired in the openings of the suras and in Qurʾān and Furqān, linking visible power with the knowledge that discloses it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r12.anchor: ولذلك أقيم المفصل من القرى بحرفي قاف ونون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r13.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r13.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that people of Paradise first eat from the bull that grazed at the edges of Paradise; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r13.anchor: أول ما يطعمه أهل الجنة من الثور الذي عليه الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r14.claim: The bull represents toil and labor on which earthly life rests; eating it in Paradise rewards people for worldly effort and releases them from the burden of earning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r14.anchor: لأن صورة الثور هي معنى ما هو الكد والكدح وجهد العمل في الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r15.claim: The added liver portion represents the people’s share of foundational knowledge; their good original intention in religion is honored, and after eating both they enter repose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p92/r15.anchor: وأضيف لذلك زيادة كبد النون التي هي صورة حظهم نم أصل العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r1.claim: Qāf signifies strength, domination, and power; nūn makes that power intelligible through the light of knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r1.anchor: ما أتقنه بحكمته من ثناء المفصل القرآني على حرفي القاف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r2.claim: The expansive Quranic portion serves learned people with rulings, stories, and difficult verses; short suras carry selected lessons suited to general listeners.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r2.anchor: ضمن ما عدا المفصل منه الذي هو من قاف إلى خاتمة الكتاب العزيز

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r3.claim: Suras opened by encompassing, unseen letters have outward meanings for the wider community and inward meanings reserved for the Prophet’s family.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r3.anchor: والسور المفتتحة بالحروف العلية الإحاطة الغيبية المنحى المستندة إلى آحاد الأعداد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r4.claim: The mufassal repeats stories, admonitions, laws, reports, and judgment in many short suras so ordinary listeners can hear and absorb lessons from longer suras, including in obligatory prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r4.anchor: ذكر فيها من أطراف القصص والمواعظ والأحكام والأنباء وأمر الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r5.claim: Qāf fittingly opens the mufassal: its numerical progression from one to ten and a hundred signals encompassing scope, and its power imagery suits public governance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r5.anchor: فكان أحق ما افتتح به مفصلهم حرف القاف الذي هو وتر الآحاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r6.claim: The Prophet often recited Sūrat Qāf in the Friday sermon, presenting the mufassal’s powerful opening to a general audience at communal prayer; no grading is given.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r6.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يكثر أن يقرأ في خطبة الجمعة سورة ( ق )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r7.claim: Sūrat Nūn pairs with Qāf by making its power manifest and adding knowledge that encompasses public affairs; power without knowledge can do more harm than good.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p93/r7.anchor: وشفعت بسورة ( ن ) المظهرة ظاهر ( ق )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r1.speaker: بعض السلف
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r1.claim: An unnamed early authority says authority unsupported by knowledge ends in humiliation; no grading applies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r1.anchor: قال بعض السلف : كل عز لم يوطده علم فإلى ذل يؤول

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r2.claim: The twenty-nine letter-opened suras encode nine ranks and a tenth that gathers and multiplies them, forming an encompassing structure throughout the Quran’s short suras.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r2.anchor: كان جميع السورة التسع والعشرين المفتتحة بالحروف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r3.claim: Qāf and nūn jointly contain the Quranic portion addressed especially to the public, through the visible mountain surrounding earth and the hidden fish beneath it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r3.anchor: كذلك كان سورة ( ق ) وسورة ( ن ) قواما خاصا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r4.claim: The letter-opened suras distinguish the Quran from earlier books by its comprehensive, final scope and the corresponding range of its contents.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r4.anchor: وبهذه السورة المفتتحة بالحروف ظهر اختصاص القرآن وتميز عن سائر الكتب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r5.claim: All interpretations of the disconnected letters are valid within their encompassing implications, including divine, angelic, prophetic, created, oath, sura-opening, and numerical readings tied to outward or inward events.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r5.anchor: كل ما فسرت به من معنى يرجع إلى مقتضاها صحيحا في إحاطتها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r6.claim: Because these letters are independent and encompassing, they need no fixed syntactic place or case ending; any nominative, accusative, or genitive assignment is possible, unlike words whose meanings require grammatical relations.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94/r6.anchor: لا يختص بمحل مخصوص يلزمه علامة إعراب مخصوصة , فمهما قدر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r1.claim: The world’s order depends on sword and pen; nūn can mean sword, inkpot, or tablet, while the sword’s power suits Qāf and the pen’s knowledge suits this sura.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r1.anchor: ولما كان قوام هذا الوجود بالسيف والقلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r2.claim: The author associates the sword with Qāf and al-Ḥadīd’s strength and power, following intervening admonition, threat, and reminders of blessings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r2.anchor: وكان السيف قد تقدم في حيز القاف الذي افتتحت به سورة ( ق )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r3.claim: The pen is the first thing God created and commanded to write all events through Judgment Day, truly in the Preserved Tablet and figuratively on the pages of created things, thus displaying all knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r3.anchor: قلم القدرة الذي هو أول ما أبدعه الله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r4.claim: God then sealed the pen so it does not speak until Judgment Day; human writing comes from granted understanding, and the pen signifies decree and its detailed execution.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r4.anchor: ثم ختم على فيه فلم ينطق ولا ينطق إلى يوم القيامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r5.claim: The phrase may ascribe writing to the pen as a genus, personified because it performs the writers’ work, or may refer to writers by ellipsis.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r5.anchor: وجمعه وأجره مجرى أولي العلم للتعظيم لأنه فعل أفعالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r6.claim: If implied writers are intended, they may be angels writing in the clear record and Preserved Tablet, or every writer, including authors of Quraysh’s boycott document against Banū Hāshim and allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r6.anchor: إما الملائكة إن كان المراد ما كتب في الكتاب المبين واللوح المحفوظ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r7.claim: The author recalls Quraysh’s pact to boycott Banū Hāshim and their allies until they surrendered the Prophet, as an example of a written deed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r7.anchor: حتى أصحاب الصحيفة الظالمة التي تقاسموا فيها على أن يقاطعوا بني هاشم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r8.claim: Whichever reading of the writers is taken, the oath concerns what is decreed, since nothing is written except what God determined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r8.anchor: وكيف ما كان فهو إشارة إلى المقدر لأنه إنما يسطر ما قضى به وحكم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r15.claim: Biqāʿī maps nūn to governing speech, the pen to universal effective decree, and writing to detailed, irrevocable destiny unfolding according to decree.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r15.anchor: فقد اشتمل الكلام التدبيري المشار إليه بالنون والقضاء الكلي التأثيري المشار إليه بالقلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r16.claim: A waterwheel illustrates the sequence: an engineer plans its parts, builders execute the plan, then the ox, wheel, and channels operate according to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r16.anchor: ومثال ذلك أن من أراد بناء دولاب احتاج أولا إلى مهندس يدبر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r17.claim: The decreed outcome divides into wretched and blessed; judgment is hidden and remains one of God’s secrets.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r17.anchor: فالحكم باطن وهو سر من أسراره سبحانه وتعالى

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan and has fifty-two verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Meccan sura openings were written in Mecca and God could add to them; he lists al-Alaq, al-Muzzammil, and al-Muddaththir among the first revelations.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: كانت إذا نزلت فاتحة سورة بمكة كتبت بمكة ثم يزيد الله فيها ما شاء

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat Nun wa-al-Qalam was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: نزلت سورة {ن والقلم} بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that God first created the pen and commanded it to record destiny through the Resurrection; he then describes the throne on water, the heavens from its vapor, earth on the fish Nun, and mountains stabilizing it.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن أول شيء خلق الله القلم فقال له: اكتب فقال: يارب وما أكتب

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet’s report that God first created pen and fish; the pen wrote everything to the Resurrection, and Nun means fish while qalam means pen.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن أول ما خلق الله القلم والحوت قال: اكتب

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r6.claim: Ubada ibn al-Samit reports the Prophet saying God first created the pen and commanded it to write all that would exist forever; al-Tirmidhi graded the report sound.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r6.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن أول ما خلق الله القلم فقال له: اكتب

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r7.claim: Qurra ibn Muawiya transmits his father’s report of the Prophet explaining the verse as a tablet of light and a pen of light writing all that will be until Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r7.anchor: عن معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} قال: لوح من نور

DURR-FULL:v8p240/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created Nun, meaning the inkwell, and the pen, which wrote everything until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v8p240/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله خلق النون وهي الدواة وخلق القلم فقال: اكتب

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r1.claim: In a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Nūn is the Preserved Tablet and the pen is from shining light.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: النون اللوح المحفوظ والقلم من نور ساطع

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r2.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the pen was created first, then Nūn as an inkwell; the pen recorded all future deeds, traces, and provisions through Judgment Day, was sealed, and then intellect was created.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن أول شيء خلق الله القلم ثم خلق النون

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Nūn is the inkwell and the pen is the pen.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {ن والقلم} قال: ن الدواة والقلم القلم

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās treats Nūn as resembling an oath sworn by God and says it is one of God's names.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله: {ن} أشبها هذا قسم الله وهي من أسماء الله

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r5.speaker: قتادة والحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r5.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan identify Nūn as an inkwell.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r5.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله: {ن} قالا: الدواة

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies Nūn as the fish on which the earth rests.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {ن} قال: هو الحوت الذي عليه الأرض

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r7.claim: Mujāhid says Nūn is the fish beneath the seventh earth and the pen wrote the Preserved Record.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الحوت الذي تحت الأرض السابعة والقلم الذي كتب به الذكر

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the pen, then the inkwell Nūn and Tablet, and recorded all future creation, deeds, and lawful or unlawful provisions before creating the heavens.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم فأخذه بيمينه وكلتا يديه يمين وخلق النون

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r9.claim: Qatāda calls the pen a great blessing: without it religion would not stand and life would not be well ordered; God knows what benefits creation.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r9.anchor: عن قتادة قال: القلم نعمة من الله عظيمة لولا القلم ما قام دين ولم يصلح عيش

DURR-FULL:v8p241/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God commanded the pen to flow and record everything through Judgment Day, then created the fish Nūn, placed the earth on it, and recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p241/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} قال: خلق الله القلم فقال: أجره فجرى بما هو كائن

DURR-FULL:v8p242/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r1.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies Nūn as the fish bearing the earths, the pen as the instrument recording God's decree in all its good, evil, benefit, and harm, and the writers as the noble recording angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ن والقلم} قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: النون السمكة التي عليها قرار الأرضين

DURR-FULL:v8p242/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “what they write” means what they write down; Mujāhid and Qatāda transmit the same explanation.
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما يسطرون} قال: وما يكتبون

DURR-FULL:v8p242/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r3.claim: A second explanation from Ibn ʿAbbās takes “what they write” to mean what they do.
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وما يسطرون} قال: وما يعملون

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the Pen and commanded it to write destiny, which runs until the Hour; water vapor formed the heavens, light spread over the earth resting on a whale, and mountains stabilized it after the whale moved.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : ان اول شيء خلق الله القلم ، فقال له اكتب ، فقال يا رب وما اكتب ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains what is written as what people know.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : وما يسطرون قال : وما يعلمون .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r3.claim: The Prophet says the hoarding miser, coarse brute, and base gluttonous oppressor do not enter Paradise; their traits are illustrated through 70:15–16 and 3:159.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3364/r3.anchor: حدثني عبد الرحمن بن غنم ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r1.claim: The written sign ن represents the named letter نون rather than spelling out its three letters, although writing normally follows pronunciation by writing a word’s component letters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r1.anchor: ورسموا حرف { ن } بصورته التي يرسم بها في الخط وهي مسمى اسمه الذي هو { نون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r2.claim: Letters in the disconnected openings are read by their names, not spelled out, as discussed at the start of al-Baqarah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r2.anchor: وإنما يقرأ باسم الحرف لا بهجائه كما تقدم في أول سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r3.claim: The name نون is pronounced with a vowelless final ن, as words are before inflection; this is also the reading in the mutawatir recitations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r3.anchor: وينطق باسم نون ساكن الآخر سكون الكلمات قبل دخول العوامل عليها ، وكذلك قرىء في القراءات المتواترة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r4.claim: Divine oaths follow the pattern of swearing by exalted things that reveal traces of God’s attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r4.anchor: يجري القسم هنا على سنن الأقسام الصادرة في كلام الله تعالى أن تكون بأشياء معظمة دالة على آثار صفات الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r5.claim: One proposed referent is a pen that stands for God’s knowledge of existing and future things, or an unseen entity known only to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r5.anchor: قيل هو ما يكنى عنه بالقلم من تعلق علم الله بالموجودات الكائنة والتي ستكون ، أو هو كائن غيبي لا يعلمه إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r6.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r6.claim: Mujāhid and Qatādah identify it as the writing pen in 96:4–5; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers this because it fits وما يسطرون and the polytheist audience’s familiar writing tool.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r6.anchor: وعن مجاهد وقتادة : أنه القلم الذي في قوله تعالى : { الذي علم بالقلم علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r7.claim: The oath forecasts that Islam’s Quran will be written and read among Muslims; the Prophet therefore directed his Companions to record revelation, and القلم is definite generically.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r7.anchor: ومن فوائد هذا القسم أن هذا القرآن كتاب الإسلام ، وأنه سيكون مكتوبا مقروءا بين المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r8.claim: The pen is honored because it writes the Quran, sacred books, and works of education, virtue, and knowledge; its mention at the start of the first revealed surah supports its honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r8.anchor: فالقسم بالقلم لشرفه بأنه يكتب به القرآن وكتبت به الكتب المقدسة وتكتب به كتب التربية ومكارم الأخلاق والعلوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r9.claim: At the surface level, وما يسطرون denotes the lines written with the pen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p59/r9.anchor: و { ما يسطرون } هي السطور المكتوبة بالقلم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r1.claim: ما may be a relative pronoun meaning what they write on pages, or a verbal noun meaning their act of writing lines.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r1.anchor: و { ما } يجوز أن تكون موصولة ، أي وما يكتبونه من الصحف ، ويجوز أن تكون مصدرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r2.claim: Another reading takes the oath as covering the pens used to write Quranic revelation and the act of writing; the Quran is thereby sworn to be unlike a madman’s speech, as in the oath by the clear Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قسما بالأقلام التي يكتب بها كتاب الوحي القرآن ، { وما يسطرون } قسما بكتابتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r3.claim: سطر means to write several words into rows; it derives from السطر, cutting, because rows of writing look like cut segments, with Abū Tammām cited as poetic evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r3.anchor: ويسطرون } : مضارع سطر ، يقال : سطر من باب نصر ، إذا كتب كلمات عدة تحصل منها صفوف من الكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r4.speaker: أبو تمام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites an Abū Tammām poetic fragment in connection with the word’s writing and row imagery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r4.anchor: وتنظيره بقول أبي تمام : وثناياكك إنها أغريض . . . البيت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r5.claim: The unexpressed subject of يسطرون is understood from the mention of the pen; the actual target is what is written, with the verbal noun used for its object and an implicit passive sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r5.anchor: وضمير { يسطرون } راجع إلى غير مذكور في الكلام وهو معلوم للسامعين لأن ذكر القلم ينبىء بكتبة يكتبون به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r6.claim: For those who take القلم as God’s knowledge, the writers are angels recording what God orders, for action or exact transmission without addition or omission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r6.anchor: ومن فسر { القلم } بمعنى تعلق علم الله تعالى بما سيكون جعل ضمير { يسطرون } راجعا إلى الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r7.claim: The pen and writing point to the real cause of the attackers’ taunts: the Book brought by the Messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r7.anchor: وأوثر القسم بالقلم والكتابة للإيماء إلى أن باعث الطاعنين على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم واللامزين له بالجنون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r8.claim: The oath denies that the Prophet is mad and consoles him against the polytheists’ taunt; Quranic denials of madness answer their claims, including the closing verse of this surah and 81:22.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r8.anchor: والمقسم عليه نفي أن يكون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مجنونا والخطاب له بهذا تسلية له لئلا يحزنه قول المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r9.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says al-Zamakhsharī made an error in his discussion here, though this passage does not restate the error’s details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p60/r9.anchor: وقد زل فيه صاحب ( الكشاف ) زلة لا تليق بعلمه .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r1.claim: Most exegetes treat ن as a disconnected letter and apply disagreements found at other sura openings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r1.anchor: ن حرف مقطع في قول الجمهور من المفسرين، فيدخله من الخلاف ما يدخل أوائل السور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās say Nūn names the great fish that bears the seven earths, according to a report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r2.anchor: ويختص هذا الموضع من الأقوال بأن قال مجاهد وابن عباس: نون، اسم الحوت الأعظم الذي عليه الأرضون السبع فيما يروى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say nūn means an inkpot, a dialect word or Arabized foreign term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك: النون اسم للدواة، فهذا إما أن يكون لغة لبعض العرب، أو تكون لفظة أعجمية عربت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r4.claim: An anonymous poet's verse says the nūn casts streaming tears, cited for inkpot usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: [الوافر] إذا ما الشوق برح بي إليهم ... ألقت النون بالدمع السجوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.claim: If ن means the fish, the pen is what God created and commanded to record events, and “they write” refers to angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.anchor: فمن قال إنه اسم الحوت جعل «القلم» الذي خلقه الله تعالى وأمره فكتب الكائنات وجعل الضمير في يسطرون للملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.claim: If ن means an inkpot, the pen is the familiar human pen and “they write” refers to people, as Ibn ʿAbbās states.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.anchor: ومن قال بأن «نون» اسم للدواة، جعل «القلم» هذا المتعارف بأيدي الناس. نص ذلك ابن عباس وجعل الضمير في يسطرون للناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r7.claim: On the inkpot reading, the oath gathers knowledge and worldly and otherworldly affairs; the pen is the tongue's sibling, intelligence's vehicle, and a universal blessing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r7.anchor: فجاء القسم على هذا بمجموع أم الكتاب الذي هو قوام للعلوم والمعارف وأمور الدنيا والآخرة، فإن القلم أخ اللسان، ومطية الفطنة، ونعمة من الله عامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r8.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r8.claim: Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra reports the Prophet said Nūn is a tablet of light.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r8.anchor: وروى معاوية بن قرة، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ن لوح من نور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Nūn is a letter of al-Raḥmān, alongside alif-lām-rā and ḥā-mīm sequences.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: هو حرف من حروف الرحمن، وقالوا إنه تقطع في القرآن: الر [يونس: 1، هود: 1، يوسف: 1، إبراهيم: 1، الحجر: 1] وحم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r10.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads نونا in the accusative, “mention Nūn,” supporting its use as the feminine sura name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بخلاف «نون» بالنصب، والمعنى: اذكر نون، وهذا يقوى مع أن يكون اسما للسورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r11.claim: As a feminine proper name for the sura, Nūn is definite and feminine and indeclinable; Nūḥ declines because three-letter brevity outweighs foreignness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r11.anchor: فهو مؤنث سمي به مؤنث، ففيه تأنيث وتعريف، ولذلك لم ينصرف، وانصرف نوح، لأن الخفة بكونه على ثلاثة أحرف غلبت على العجمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and al-Ḥasan read Nūn with kasra, like an oath by God or in جبر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r1.anchor: ابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق والحسن: «نون» بكسر النون، وهذا كما تقول في القسم بالله، وكما تقول: «جبر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r2.claim: Some explain the kasra as avoiding two consecutive unvoweled letters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r2.anchor: والحسن: «نون» بكسر النون، وهذا كما تقول في القسم بالله، وكما تقول: «جبر» وقيل كسرت لاجتماع الساكنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ read Nūn with sukūn as a separate letter to pause on.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم: «نون» بسكون النون، وهذا على أنه حرف منفصل فحقه الوقوف عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r4.speaker: قوم منهم الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r4.claim: Some reciters, including al-Kisāʾī, assimilate Nūn into the following wāw without nasalization.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r4.anchor: وقرأ قوم، منهم الكسائي: ن والقلم بالإدغام دون غنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r5.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r5.claim: Other reciters assimilate it with nasalization.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r6.speaker: الكسائي ويعقوب عن نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Yaʿqūb from Nāfiʿ, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim use concealment between assimilation and clear pronunciation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r6.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ويعقوب عن نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالإخفاء بين الإدغام والإظهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r7.claim: يسطرون means writing lines: angels write deeds and commands; humans write revealed books, knowledge, and similar things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r7.anchor: ويسطرون معناه: يكتبون سطورا، فإن أراد الملائكة فهو كتب الأعمال وما يؤمرون به، وإن أراد بني آدم، فهي الكتب المنزلة والعلوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو، ابن عامر، حمزة، حفص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the final nūn of the letter name clearly before wāw; al-Farrāʾ preferred this reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص ن والقلم النون في آخر الهجاء من نون ظاهرة عندالواو وهذا اختيار الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r2.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم، الكسائي، خلف، يعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reports that ʿĀṣim did not pronounce the nūn of Nūn distinctly; al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf, and Yaʿqūb read likewise, as al-Zajjāj preferred.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r2.anchor: وروى أبو بكر عن عاصم أنه كان لا يبين النون من نون وبها قرأ الكسائي وخلف ويعقوب وهو اختيار الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو رزين، قتادة، الأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r3.claim: They read Nūn with a kasra on the nūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو رزين وقتادة والأعمش نون والقلم بكسر النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r4.speaker: الحسن، أبو عمران، أبو نهيك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r4.claim: They read Nūn with a ḍamma on the nūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو عمران وأبو نهيك ن والقلم برفع النون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God first created the Pen, then Nūn, meaning the inkwell; Ibn al-Jawzī gives no grading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r5.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أول ما خلق الله القلم ثم خلق النون وهي الدواة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r6.claim: In Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s report from Ibn ʿAbbās and in the views of al-Ḥasan and Qatāda, Nūn means an inkwell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r6.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير وبه قال الحسن وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r7.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r7.claim: Nūn is the final letter of the name al-Raḥmān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه آخر حروف الرحمن رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r8.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي، ابن السائب، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r8.claim: Nūn is the whale on the back of the earth, according to a report from Ibn ʿAbbās and the named exegetes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r8.anchor: أنه الحوت الذي على ظهر الأرض وهذا المعنى في رواية أبي ظبيان عن ابن عباس وهو مذهب مجاهد والسدي وابن السائب ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r9.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r9.claim: Nūn is a tablet of light.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r9.anchor: والرابع أنه لوح من نور قاله معاوية بن قرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r10.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r10.claim: Nūn begins the divine names Naṣīr and Nāṣir.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r10.anchor: والخامس أنه افتتاح اسمه نصير وناصر قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r11.speaker: القرظي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r11.claim: Nūn is an oath by God's support for the believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r11.anchor: والسادس أنه قسم بنصرة الله للمؤمنين قاله القرظي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r12.claim: Nūn is a river in Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r12.anchor: والسابع أنه نهر في الجنة قاله جعفر الصادق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r13.speaker: author
