IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r13.claim: The Pen may be the one used to write on the Preserved Tablet or the one people use for writing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r13.anchor: وفي القلظم قولان أحدهما أنه الذي كتب به في اللوح المحفوظ والثاني أنه الذي يكتب به الناس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r14.claim: God swears by the Pen because writings are made with it; yasṭurūn means “they write.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r14.anchor: وإنما أقسم به الأن كتبه إنما تكتب ويسطرون بمعنى يكتبون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r15.claim: Those who write may be angels; what they write is either the remembrance, according to Mujāhid and al-Suddī, or human deeds, according to Muqātil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r15.anchor: وفي المشار إليهم قولان أحدهما أنهم الملائكة وفيما أرادوا بما يكتبونه قولان أحدهما أنه الذكر قاله مجاهد والسدي والثاني أعمال بني آدم قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r16.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r16.claim: An alternative view is that the writers are all those who write.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p326/r16.anchor: والقول الثاني أنهم جميع الكتبة حكاه الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir refers back to his discussion of the disconnected letters at the start of al-Baqara, saying Nun is like Sad and Qaf and that the earlier treatment makes repetition unnecessary.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم الكلام على حروف الهجاء في أول "سورة البقرة"، وأن قوله: {ن} كقوله: {ص} {ق}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r2.claim: One view takes Nun to be a huge whale in the vast surrounding current, bearing the seven earths.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: المراد بقوله: {ن} حوت عظيم على تيار الماء العظيم المحيط،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r3.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, God first creates the Pen and commands it to write destiny through the Day of Resurrection; He then creates Nun, raises water vapor from it to form the sky, and spreads the earth on its back. When Nun moves, mountains fix the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم قال: اكتب. قال: وما أكتب؟ قال: اكتب القدر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r4.claim: A second Ibn Abbas version says God first created the Pen, which wrote all things until the Resurrection, then created Nun above the water and compressed the earth onto it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي الضحى، عن ابن عباس قال: إن أول شيء خلق ربي، عز وجل، القلم، ثم قال له: اكتب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a marfu report from Ibn Abbas that God first created the Pen and the whale, told the Pen to write everything until the Resurrection, and identified Nun as the whale and the Pen as the Pen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p184#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن أول ما خلق الله القلم والحوت، قال للقلم: اكتب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r1.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says God first created the Pen and then Nun, identified here as an inkpot; the Pen wrote deeds, livelihood, traces, and lifespans until the Resurrection, was sealed, and was followed by the creation of the intellect.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن أول شيء خلقه الله القلم، ثم خلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r2.claim: Mujahid reports the view that Nun is the great fish beneath the seventh earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كان يقال: النون: الحوت [العظيم]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r3.speaker: البغوي وجماعة من المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r3.claim: Al-Baghawi and other commentators say a rock as thick as the heavens and earth rests on the whale, a bull with forty thousand horns rests on that rock, and the seven earths lie on the bull; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r3.anchor: وذكر البغوي وجماعة من المفسرين: إن على ظهر هذا الحوت صخرة سمكها كغلظ السموات والأرض،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir calls it strange that some commentators apply this cosmological whale story to the authentic report that Paradise's first food is an extra portion of a whale's liver.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r4.anchor: ومن العجيب (7) أن بعضهم حمل على هذا المعنى الحديث الذي رواه الإمام أحمد:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r5.claim: In the report of Abdullah ibn Salam's questions, the Prophet says the first sign of the Hour is a fire driving people from east to west, the first food of Paradise is extra whale liver, and a child's resemblance follows whichever parent's fluid prevails; the report is in al-Bukhari and Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r5.anchor: عن أنس: أن عبد الله بن سلام بلغه مقدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، فأتاه فسأله عن أشياء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r6.claim: In Muslim's report from Thawban, a rabbi asks about Paradise's welcome gift and food and drink: the Prophet answers extra whale liver, a bull of Paradise, then water from a spring called Salsabil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p185/r6.anchor: عن ثوبان: أن حبرا سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن مسائل، فكان منها أن قال: فما تحفتهم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r1.claim: A mursal, gharīb report says Nun and the Pen are a tablet of light and a Pen of light that writes what will happen until the Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r1.anchor: عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {ن والقلم وما يسطرون} لوح من نور، وقلم من نور،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says he was informed that the luminous Pen is one hundred years long.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج (4) أخبرت أن ذلك القلم من نور طوله مائة عام.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify Nun as an inkpot, while the Pen is the writing implement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله: {ن} قالا هي الدواة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r4.claim: A marfu report from Abu Hurayra says God created Nun, meaning the inkpot; Ibn Kathir calls this report very strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "خلق الله النون، وهي الدواة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God created the inkpot Nun and the Pen and ordered the Pen to record every deed, good or evil, and every lawful or unlawful provision, with each person's earthly course and lifespan. Angels copy each day's deeds from the record; after provision, traces, and lifespan end, they find the person has died and no further deeds remain on the register.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله خلق النون -وهي الدواة-وخلق القلم، فقال: اكتب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas argues that the Arabic verb for copying means transcription from an original, using the angels' statement that they copied people's deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p186/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ألستم قوما عربا تسمعون الحفظة يقولون: {إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r1.claim: The apparent sense is the generic writing pen, as in the passage about God teaching by the Pen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r1.anchor: الظاهر أنه جنس القلم الذي يكتب به كقوله {اقرأ وربك الأكرم الذي علم بالقلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r2.claim: God swears by the Pen and calls attention to the blessing of teaching writing, through which knowledge is acquired.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r2.anchor: فهو قسم منه تعالى، وتنبيه لخلقه على ما أنعم به عليهم من تعليم الكتابة التي بها تنال العلوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada gloss the phrase as what people write.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة: يعني: وما يكتبون.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r4.claim: A report through Abu al-Duha from Ibn Abbas instead glosses it as what people do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الضحى، عن ابن عباس: {وما يسطرون} أي: وما يعملون.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the phrase refers to angels and what they write down of people's deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: {وما يسطرون} يعني الملائكة وما تكتب من أعمال العباد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r6.speaker: آخرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r6.claim: Another view identifies the Pen as the one God used to record the decrees fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل المراد هاهنا بالقلم الذي أجراه الله بالقدر حين كتب مقادير الخلائق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r7.claim: Ubadah ibn al-Samit reports the Prophet saying the Pen was God's first creation and was ordered to write destiny, past and future forever; Ibn Kathir notes Ahmad's multiple routes and al-Tirmidhi's grading of hasan, sahih, gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r7.anchor: دعاني أبي حين حضره الموت فقال: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r8.claim: A separate report from Ibn Abbas says the Pen was the first thing created and wrote everything; Ibn Kathir calls this route gharīb and says the compilers did not transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أنه كان يحدث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أول شيء خلقه الله القلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Pen is the one used to write al-Dhikr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {والقلم} يعني: الذي كتب به الذكر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir reiterates that the phrase means what they write.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.anchor: وقوله: {وما يسطرون} أي: يكتبون كما تقدم.

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r1.claim: The Meccan sūra is called Sūrat Nūn or al-Qalam and has fifty-two verses.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r1.anchor: مكية وتسمى سورة (القلم) وهي اثنتان وخمسون آية

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r2.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r2.claim: A report from Ubayy says recitation earns the reward of those whose character God made excellent; no grading is stated.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r2.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (ن والقلم) أعطاه الله تعالى ثواب الذين حسن الله أخلاقهم

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r3.claim: Al-Mulk closed with the disbelievers' denial and threat, and this sūra opens with the same themes.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r3.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (الملك) بذكر تكذيب الكفار ووعيدهم، افتتح هذه السورة بمثل ذلك.

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وحمزة
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r4.claim: These readers pronounce the nūn clearly before wāw; Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī conceal it, and reports differ for Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqūb.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وحمزة: نون بإظهار النون عند الواو، وقرأ ابن عامر والكسائي بإخفاء النون

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r5.claim: The apparent reading gives the disjoint letter sukūn because such letters are always read with sukūn; Ibn ʿAbbās supplies an oath particle and reads kasra.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r5.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة بالجزم؛ لأنها من حروف الهجاء، وهي مجزومة أبدا، وعن ابن عباس بالكسر على إضمار حرف القسم

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r6.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r6.claim: ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar reads fatḥa, supplying an imperative (“recite Nūn”); it is an oath answered by verse 68:2.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r6.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بالفتح على إضمار فعل، أي: اقرأ نون وهو قسم، وجواب القسم: (ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون)

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r7.claim: Saṭr means writing; its plurals are suṭūr and asṭur.
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r7.anchor: السطر: الكتابة، سطر يسطر سطرا: إذا كتب، وجمع السطر: سطور وأسطر.

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومقاتل وعطاء والسدي والكلبي والواقدي
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r6.claim: These authorities say Nūn is the whale supporting the earths.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r6.anchor: قيل: هو الحوت الذي عليه الأرضون، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، ومقاتل، وعطاء، والسدي، والكلبي، والواقدي

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r7.claim: A differing report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes Nūn as a letter from al-Raḥmān.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو حرف من حروف الرحمن، عن ابن عباس بخلاف

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r8.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن عباس والأصم
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and a differing Ibn ʿAbbās report interpret Nūn as an inkwell; this is also al-Aṣamm's view.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r8.anchor: وقيل: النون: الدواة، عن الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وابن عباس بخلاف، وهو قول الأصم

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r9.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r9.claim: Muʿāwiya b. Qurra transmits from the Prophet that Nūn is a tablet of light.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r9.anchor: وقيل: (ن) لوح من نور، عن معاوية بن قرة رفعه إلى النبي

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says Nūn is an object by which God swears.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو قسم أقسم الله به، عن ابن زيد

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r11.claim: Ibn Kaysān says Nūn is the opening of the sūra.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r11.anchor: وقيل: فاتحة السورة، عن ابن كيسان

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r12.speaker: عطاء
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r12.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says it opens divine names beginning with nūn: Nāṣir, Naṣīr, and Nūr.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r12.anchor: وقيل: افتتاح أسمائه: ناصر ونصير ونور، عن عطاء

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r13.speaker: الصادق
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r13.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says Nūn is a river in Paradise.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r13.anchor: وقيل: نهر في الجنة، عن الصادق

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r14.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Nūn is the name of the sūra.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r14.anchor: وقيل: اسم للسورة، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r15.claim: Abū Muslim says the opening signals that the Qurʾān is composed of these letters, which people cannot match, demonstrating its miraculous character.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r15.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى أن القرآن مركب من هذه الحروف، ويتعذر عليكم مثلها لتعلموا أنه معجز، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r16.speaker: أبو بكر الزبيري
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r16.claim: Abū Bakr al-Zubayrī says the letters indicate the Qurʾān is composed of them and is created.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r16.anchor: وقيل: إشارة إلى أنه مركب منها ليعلم أنه محدث، عن أبي بكر الزبيري

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r17.speaker: أبو علي قطرب
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r17.claim: Abū ʿAlī Quṭrub links the opening to Quraysh's call not to listen to the Qurʾān: these letters make them listen, so what follows establishes the proof.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r17.anchor: وقيل: قالوا: (لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه) فافتتح السورة بهذه الحروف ليستمعوا، فيأتي ما بعده إلزاما وتأكيدا للحجة

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r18.claim: Another view takes Nūn as a sea whale and divine sign: it dies outside water, just as land animals die in water, demonstrating God's power.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r18.anchor: وقيل: المراد به الحوت في البحر، وهو من آيات الله تعالى؛ إذ خلقه في الماء، فإذا فارق الماء مات

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r19.claim: The wāw is an oath; one view swears by the pen to magnify its importance as a second human tongue that conveys thoughts, reaches the distant, preserves books, and sustains religion and worldly order.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r19.anchor: والقلم الواو واو القسم، قيل: أقسم بالقلم تنبيها على عظم شأنه؛ لأنه أحد لساني الإنسان، يؤدي عنه ما في ضميره

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r20.claim: Another view contrasts lasting writing with speech: hand-writing survives the passing days, while spoken expression fades over years.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r20.anchor: وقيل: البيان اثنان: بيان اللسان، وبيان البنان، ثم بيان البنان يبقى على مرور الأيام، وبيان اللسان يندرس على مرور الأعوام

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r21.claim: A report says the first thing God created was the pen, which writes what will happen until the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r21.anchor: وقيل: أول ما خلق الله تعالى القلم يجري بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r22.claim: Another view identifies it as a pen of light as long as the distance between heaven and earth.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r22.anchor: وقيل: هو قلم من نور، طوله ما بين السماء والأرض

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r23.claim: Another view takes the pen as writing and script through which God taught servants, as in “He taught by the pen.”
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r23.anchor: وقيل: أزاد بالقلم الخط والكتابة التي مر على عباده حيث علمهم بقوله: (علم بالقلم)

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r24.claim: Another view understands the oath as being by the Lord of Nūn and the Lord of the pen.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r24.anchor: وقيل: القسم برب نون، ورب القلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r25.claim: One explanation of “what they write” is what is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r25.anchor: وما يسطرون أي: ما يكتبون، قيل: ما يكتب في اللوح المحفوظ

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r26.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r26.claim: Abū ʿAlī says it is what recording angels write of people's deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r26.anchor: وقيل: ما تسطره الحفظة من أعمال العباد، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v10p7022/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r27.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r27.claim: Abū Muslim says it includes everything written by all scribes, human and otherwise.
JISHUMI:v10p7022/r27.anchor: وقيل: ما يكتبه جميع الكتبة بنو آدم وغيرهم، عن أبي مسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r1.claim: The opening letter is read with clear articulation or assimilation, and with nūn quiescent, open, or kasra-marked, as in Ṣād.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r1.anchor: قرىء : ( ن والقلم ) بالبيان والإدغام ، وبسكون النون وفتحها وكسرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r2.claim: The intended ن is the alphabetic letter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r2.anchor: والمراد هذا الحرف من حروف المعجم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r3.claim: The proposed meaning ‘inkpot’ is challenged: neither its status as a common noun nor as a proper name fits the expected case marking and place in the sentence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r3.anchor: وأما قولهم : هو الدواة فما أدري أهو وضع لغوي أم شرعي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r4.claim: If ن meant an inkpot in an oath, a common noun would need genitive and nunation, while a proper name would need its appropriate genitive or fatḥa marking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r4.anchor: فإن قلت : هو مقسم به وجب إن كان جنسا أن تجره وتنونه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r5.claim: The interpretation of ن as a fish, whether one fish or the alleged Bahamut, faces the same grammatical problem as the inkpot interpretation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r5.anchor: وكذلك التفسير بالحوت : إما أن يراد نون من النينان ، أو يجعل علما للبهموت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r6.claim: The proposed interpretations ‘a tablet of light or gold’ and ‘a river in Paradise’ likewise do not fit the syntax.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r6.anchor: والتفسير باللوح من نور أو ذهب ، والنهر في الجنة نحو ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r7.claim: God swears by the pen to honor it, since its creation and design show great wisdom and its benefits are beyond description.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r7.anchor: وأقسم بالقلم : تعظيما له ، لما في خلقه وتسويته من الدلالة على الحكمة العظيمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r8.claim: ما يسطرون can mean the books people write or what the recording angels write; ما can be relative or a verbal noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r8.anchor: وما يكتب من كتب وقيل ما يستره الحفظة وما موصولة أو مصدرية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r9.claim: Alternatively, ‘the pen’ refers to its users, so the pronoun in يسطرون refers to them and means the people of the pen and their written lines, including all writers or the recording angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالقلم أصحابه فيكون الضمير في { يسطرون } لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r1.claim: In Abu al-Duha's report from Ibn Abbas, raised to the Prophet, nūn is the whale that carries the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن النون الحوت الذي عليه الأرض , قاله ابن عباس من رواية أبي الضحى عنه , وقد رفعه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits from the Prophet that nūn is the inkwell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r2.anchor: الثاني : أن النون الدواة , رواه أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r3.claim: In a report through al-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas says nūn is a letter from the name al-Rahman.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r3.anchor: الثالث : أنه حرف من حروف الرحمن , قاله ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك عنه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r4.speaker: معاوية بن قرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r4.claim: Muawiya ibn Qurra reports from his father, from the Prophet, that nūn is a tablet of light.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r4.anchor: الرابع : هو لوح من نور , رواه معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r5.claim: Another transmitted view treats nūn as the name of the surah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r5.anchor: الخامس : أنه اسم من أسماء السورة , وهو مأثور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r6.claim: Nūn is an object by which God swears, and God may swear by whatever He wills.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r6.anchor: السادس : أنه قسم أقسم الله به , ولله تعالى أن يقسم بما يشاء , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r7.claim: One view is that nūn is a letter of the alphabet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r7.anchor: السابع : أنه حرف من حروف المعجم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak gives the Persian expression أيذون كن as the meaning of nūn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r8.anchor: الثامن : أن نون بالفارسية أيذون كن , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r9.claim: If no transmitted explanation is established, nūn may signify the bringing of acts into being, paired with the pen and what is written as an oath about God's acts and words.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r9.anchor: ويحتمل تاسعا : إن لم يثبت به نقل أن يكون معناه : تكوين الأفعال والقلم وما يسطرون , فنزل الأقوال جميعا في قسمه بين أفعاله وأقواله , وهذا أعم قسمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r10.claim: A tenth possibility is the soul, addressed indirectly by its first letter; the pen is what God decreed for the soul of fortune or misery in the Preserved Tablet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r10.anchor: ويحتمل عاشرا : أن يريد بالنون النفس لأن الخطاب متوجه إليها بغيرعينها بأول حروفها , والمراد بالقلم ما قدره الله لها وعليها من سعادة وشقاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r11.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r11.claim: The pen is the ordinary writing instrument, a blessing and benefit for people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r11.anchor: أحدهما : أنه القلم الذي يكتبون به لأنه نعمة عليهم ومنفعة لهم , فأقسم بما أنعم , قاله ابن بحر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r12.claim: The pen writes remembrance on the Preserved Tablet; Ibn Jurayj says it is made of light and extends from heaven to earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنه القلم الذي يكتب به الذكر على اللوح المحفوظ , قال ابن جريج : هو من نور , طوله كما بين السماء والأرض .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r13.claim: What they inscribe means what they know.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r13.anchor: أحدها : وما يعلمون , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r14.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r14.claim: It means what they write of remembrance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r14.anchor: الثاني : وما يكتبون , يعني من الذكر , قاله مجاهد والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r15.claim: Alternatively, the writers are angels recording people's good and evil deeds.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r15.anchor: الثالث : أنهم الملائكة الكاتبون يكتبون أعمال الناس من خير وشر .

MUJAHID:v2p687/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p687/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p687/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Nūn means the inkwell, while the pen means the pen.
MUJAHID:v2p687/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ ن والقلم ﴾ قال النون الدواة والقلم القلم

MUJAHID:v2p687/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p687/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v2p687/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that God first created the pen and commanded it to write what would happen through Judgment Day; God then created Nūn, the fish, and flattened the earth upon it.
MUJAHID:v2p687/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أن أول ما خلق الله عز وجل القلم قال له اكتب ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

MUQATIL:68:1/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:1/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:1/r1.claim: Nun is the whale in an ocean beneath the lowest earth; the pen is made of light and writes across the space between heaven and earth on the Preserved Tablet.
MUQATIL:68:1/r1.anchor: يعني بنون الحوت وهوبحر تحت الأرض السفلى والقلم قلم من نور

MUQATIL:68:1/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:1/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:1/r2.claim: What is written is the angels' record of the deeds of Adam's descendants.
MUQATIL:68:1/r2.anchor: يقول: وما يكتب الملائكة من أعمال بني آدم

MUQATIL:68:1/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:1/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:1/r3.claim: When Abu Jahl, Utba, Shayba, and others called Muhammad insane, God swore by the whale, pen, and angels' records of human deeds.
MUQATIL:68:1/r3.anchor: وذلك حين قال كفار مكة، أبو جهل بن هشام، وعتبة بن ربيعة، وشيبة بن ربيعة وغيرهم: إن محمدا مجنون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r1.claim: The apparent meaning is the alphabetic letter nūn; its sukūn indicates a disconnected letter rather than a common or proper noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r1.anchor: فالسكون دليل على أنه من حروف المعجم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r2.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r2.claim: Al-Hasan interprets nūn as an inkwell; al-Nasafi objects that this noun would require inflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r2.anchor: قول الحسن أنه الدواة وقول ابن عباس أنه الحوت الذي عليه الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets nūn as the fish supporting the earth, named Tamhūt; al-Nasafi objects that this noun would require inflection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r3.anchor: قول ابن عباس أنه الحوت الذي عليه الأرض واسمه تهموت فمشكل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r4.claim: The pen may be the one used to write on the Tablet, the angels' pen, or a pen used by people; God swears by it for its immeasurable benefits.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r4.anchor: أي ما كتب به اللوح أو قلم الملائكة أو الذي يكتب به الناس أقسم به لما فيه من المنافع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r5.claim: “ما” may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun; what is written may be the recording angels' records or records of good deeds.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p267#7/r5.anchor: أي ما يسطره الحفظة أو ما يكتب به من الخير من كتب وما موصولة أو مصدرية

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r1.speaker: أبو بكر والمفضل وهبيرة وورش وابن محيصن وابن عامر والكسائي ويعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r1.claim: Abū Bakr, al-Mufaḍḍal, Hubayra, Warsh, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb assimilate the second nūn in the spelled name into wāw.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r1.anchor: أدغم النون الثانية في هجائها في الواو أبو بكر والمفضل وهبيرة وورش وابن محيصن

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r2.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r2.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the nūn distinctly.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r3.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads nūn with fatḥa, as though an implicit verb governs it.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r3.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بفتحها كأنه أضمر فعلا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ونصر وابن أبي إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Naṣr, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with kasra, supplied by an implicit oath preposition.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ونصر وابن أبي إسحاق بكسرها على إضمار حرف القسم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r5.speaker: هارون ومحمد ابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r5.claim: Hārūn and Muḥammad ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read it with ḍamma as a built form.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r5.anchor: وقرأ هارون ومحمد ابن السميقع بضمها على البناء

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r6.speaker: معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r6.claim: A report from Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra, raised through his father to the Prophet, says nūn is a tablet of light.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r6.anchor: فروى معاوية بن قرة عن أبيه يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «ن لوح من نور».

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r7.speaker: ثابت البناني
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r7.claim: Thābit al-Bunānī says nūn is the inkwell; al-Ḥasan and Qatāda share this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r7.anchor: وروى ثابت البناني أن «ن» الدواة. وقاله الحسن وقتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r8.claim: A lengthy report says God created the pen, then nūn as its inkwell, ordered the pen to write all events through the Resurrection, and sealed it; He then created the intellect and said He would perfect it in those He loved and diminish it in those He hated. The most intelligent are most obedient.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r8.anchor:
عن أبي هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:
" أول ما خلق الله القلم ثم خلق النون

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r9.claim: Mujāhid says nūn is the whale beneath the seventh earth and the pen is the one that wrote the Reminder.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r9.anchor: وعن مجاهد قال: «ن» الحوت الذي تحت الأرض السابعة. قال: { والقلم } الذي كتب به الذكر.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r10.speaker: مقاتل ومرة الهمداني وعطاء الخراساني والسدي والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r10.claim: Muqātil, Murra al-Hamdānī, ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, al-Suddī, and al-Kalbī say nūn is the whale that bears the earths.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r10.anchor: وكذا قال مقاتل ومرة الهمداني وعطاء الخراساني والسدي والكلبي: إن النون هو الحوت

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r11.claim: Abū Ẓabyān transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the pen first wrote what would be, water vapor rose and formed heaven, then the whale bore the earth; when it shook, mountains fixed it, and the mountains boast over earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1/r11.anchor: وروى أبو ظبيان عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما خلق الله القلم فجرى بما هو كائن

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say the whale's name is al-Bahmūt.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r1.anchor:
مالي أراكم كلكم سكوتا
والله ربي خلق البهموتا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r2.speaker: الراجز
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r2.claim: The rajaz poet's lines name the whale al-Bahmūt, attesting that name.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r2.anchor:
مالي أراكم كلكم سكوتا
والله ربي خلق البهموتا

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r3.speaker: أبو اليقظان والواقدي
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Yaqẓān and al-Wāqidī call the whale Layūthā.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r4.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r4.claim: Kaʿb gives the whale's name as Lawthūthā, then also reports the name Balhamūthā.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r5.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r5.claim: Kaʿb recounts that Satan whispered to the whale bearing the earths, and it considered casting them off; God sent a creature into its nostril and brain, the whale complained, and God let the creature out, whereupon it ceased its plan.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r5.anchor: قال كعب: إن إبليس تغلغل إلى الحوت الذي على ظهره الأرضون فوسوس في قلبه

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, reporting from Ibn ʿAbbās, says nūn is the final letter of the name al-Raḥmān; alif-lām-rā, ḥā-mīm, and nūn are its separate letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك عن ابن عباس: إن «ن» آخر حرف من حروف الرحمن. قال: الر، وحم، ون الرحمن تعالى متقطعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says nūn is an object by which God swears.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو قسم أقسم الله تعالى به.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysān says nūn opens the sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: هو فاتحة السورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r9.claim: Another view treats nūn as the name of the sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: اسم السورة. وقال عطاء وأبو العالية:

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r10.speaker: عطاء وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Abū al-ʿĀliya say nūn opens names of God such as Naṣīr, Nūr, and Nāṣir.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء وأبو العالية: هو افتتاح اسمه نصير ونور وناصر.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says God swore by His support of believers, a true promise supported by 30:47.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r11.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب: أقسم الله تعالى بنصره للمؤمنين وهو حق.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r12.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says nūn is a river of Paradise called Nūn.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r12.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق: هو نهر من أنهار الجنة يقال له نون.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r13.speaker: القشيري أبو نصر عبد الرحيم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r13.claim: Al-Qushayrī prefers taking nūn as the familiar alphabet letter: it is uninflected, whereas a full word would inflect like al-qalam, and so resembles other sūra initials; on this view it names the sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r13.anchor: وهو اختيار القشيري أبو نصر عبد الرحيم في تفسيره. قال: لأن «ن» حرف لم يعرب

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r14.claim: God swears by the pen because it conveys meaning like the tongue; the oath encompasses every writing pen in heaven and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r14.anchor: أقسم بالقلم لما فيه من البيان كاللسان وهو واقع على كل قلم مما يكتب به

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r15.speaker: أبو الفتح البستي
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r15.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ al-Bustī's poem contrasts the sword with the pen and says God's oath gives the scribal pen lasting honor and distinction.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r15.anchor:
ومنه قول أبي الفتح البستي:
إذا أقسم الأبطال يوما بسيفهم
وعدوه مما يكسب المجد والكرم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is an oath by God's created, luminous pen, as long as the distance between heaven and earth, which wrote everything destined until Resurrection on the Preserved Tablet.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذا قسم بالقلم الذي خلقه الله فأمره فجرى بكتابة جميع ما هو كائن

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r17.claim: Another account from Ibn ʿAbbās says God split the pen in two, ordered it to write, and told it to record what would happen until Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r17.anchor: ويقال. خلق الله القلم ثم نظر إليه فانشق نصفين فقال: اجر فقال: يا رب بم أجري؟

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r18.speaker: الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r18.claim: On his deathbed, al-Walīd ibn ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit says his father urged him to fear God, believe in divine oneness and predestination, then cited a Prophetic report about the pen.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1#2/r18.anchor: وقال الوليد بن عبادة بن الصامت: أوصاني أبي عند موته فقال: يا بني، اتق الله، واعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r1.claim: The Prophetic report cited by al-Walīd ibn ʿUbāda says the first created thing was the pen; God told it to write destiny, and it wrote what had happened and would happen forever.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r1.anchor: إن أول ما خلق الله القلم فقال له اكتب فقال يا رب وما أكتب فقال اكتب القدر

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first created pen wrote everything that would be, including the words “May the hands of Abū Lahab perish” (111:1).
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أول ما خلق الله القلم فأمره أن يكتب ما هو كائن فكتب فيما كتب { تبت يدآ أبي لهب }.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the pen is a blessing from God to His servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: القلم نعمة من الله تعالى على عباده.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r4.speaker: غيره
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r4.claim: Another account distinguishes the first pen, which wrote destiny in the Reminder and was placed above the Throne, from a second pen for earthly writing, discussed at 96:1.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r4.anchor: قال غيره: فخلق الله القلم الأول فكتب ما يكون في الذكر ووضعه عنده فوق عرشه

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r5.claim: Mā yasṭurūn means what they write.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وما يسطرون } أي وما يكتبون.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the writers meant are angels recording the deeds of human beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r6.anchor: يريد الملائكة يكتبون أعمال بني آدم قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r7.claim: Another view takes the writers to be people, writing and communicating with one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r7.anchor: وقيل: وما يكتبون أي الناس ويتفاهمون به.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains mā yasṭurūn as “what they know.”
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ومعنى «وما يسطرون» وما يعلمون.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r9.claim: Mā may be a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, yielding “what they write” or “their writing”; the referent may be any writers or the recording angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r9.anchor: و «ما» موصولة أو مصدرية أي ومسطوراتهم أو وسطرهم، ويراد به كل من يسطر

ITQAN:v3p299/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p299/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p299/r10.claim: Al-Ankabut, al-Rum, and Nun are exceptions to that pattern; al-Suyuti says their rationale is explained in Asrar al-Tanzil.
ITQAN:v3p299/r10.anchor: إلا ثلاثت سور العنكبوت والروم ون ليس فيها ما يتعلق به
